puzzles.title: The Confrontation
puzzles.question: Camus locates the absurd neither in the world alone nor in humans alone, but in their confrontation: our appetite for meaning meeting a silent world.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The absurd is born of the encounter — longing plus silence. Remove either term and it vanishes; divorce, not desert, is the diagnosis.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Neither a mute universe without questioners nor satisfied minds without questions produces the absurd. Camus places it precisely at the collision: the divorce between appetite and answer.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Absurdity lives in encounters, not in objects.
Longing plus silence equals the full formula.
Single-term explanations miss the confrontation.
Diagnose divorces, not deserts.
Share this: name one appetite the world leaves unanswered.

puzzles.title: The Despair Charge
puzzles.question: Because Camus starts from meaninglessness, his philosophy ultimately endorses despair and resignation as the honest response.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. The absurd diagnoses; revolt prescribes. Despair surrenders the confrontation Camus demands we maintain — lucidity without resignation is the whole ethic.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Starting from silence, Camus builds revolt, freedom, and passion — never resignation. Despair agrees with the silence; revolt answers it. The Myth's arc climbs from diagnosis to defiance.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Diagnoses are not prescriptions — check the arc.
Revolt answers what despair merely echoes.
Lucidity without resignation is the demanded stance.
Follow arguments past their first chapter.
Share this: answer one silence with action today.

puzzles.title: The Happy Condemned
puzzles.question: Camus concludes that Sisyphus — condemned to roll his rock eternally — must be imagined happy, his lucid revolt filling the struggle with meaning.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Conscious fate becomes owned fate: each descent Sisyphus chooses his rock, and the struggle itself suffices. Happiness here is defiance, not comfort.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The famous closing inverts the punishment: lucidity converts sentence into choice, and chosen struggle fills the heart. 'One must imagine Sisyphus happy' crowns revolt, not resignation.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Chosen struggle fills hearts that sentences empty.
Lucidity converts punishments into positions.
Sufficiency lives inside effort, not arrival.
Own the descent and the rock lightens.
Share this: choose one burden consciously today.

puzzles.title: The Only Door
puzzles.question: Camus argues that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem because a meaningless life logically compels self-destruction.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Suicide is the serious question precisely because Camus answers no: living without appeal refutes it. The problem is real; the compulsion is denied.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Camus opens with suicide as the fundamental question in order to reject it — the absurd must be lived, not fled. Evading the confrontation settles nothing; revolt is the argued answer.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Serious questions need not compel dark answers.
Opening with suicide frames the stakes, not the verdict.
Living-without-appeal is the argued alternative.
Read past the first sentence of every provocation.
Share this: live one question instead of fleeing it.

puzzles.title: The Second Suicide
puzzles.question: Camus rejects not only physical suicide but also 'philosophical suicide' — the leap of faith that escapes the absurd through God or absolutes.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Leaps to God, Reason, or eternity dodge the confrontation as surely as death. Camus demands the tension be kept, not dissolved by either exit.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Kierkegaard's leap and Husserl's essences both exit the absurd through transcendence — elegant evasions Camus refuses. Two suicides, one physical, one intellectual; revolt rejects both doors.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Evasions wear sacred and scholarly costumes alike.
Tension kept beats tension dissolved.
Leaps exit; revolt remains.
Suspect every exit that ends the questioning.
Share this: keep one tension unresolved this week.

puzzles.title: The Permanent No
puzzles.question: Camusian revolt means defiance without hope of final victory — a permanent 'no' to one's condition paired with living fully inside it.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Revolt refuses consolation and surrender together: no to fate, yes to life. Permanence is the point — a confrontation maintained, never won.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Revolt is not revolution (no final victory promised) but stance: lucid refusal plus passionate living. Temporary rebellion seeks outcomes; revolt is the outcome — maintained tension as a way of life.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Stances outlast campaigns when no victory exists.
Refusal plus passion defines the position.
Maintained tension is itself a way of life.
Seek no exit from the confrontation.
Share this: hold one tension without resolving it.

puzzles.title: The Answered World
puzzles.question: Even if the universe answered every human longing completely, Camus's absurd would stubbornly survive as a basic mood.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Answered longing dissolves the confrontation that births the absurd — no silence, no divorce. The absurd is conditional, not atmospheric.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The absurd needs both terms: appetite and silence. A responding world ends the divorce, and with it the concept. Conditionality is the doctrine's honesty — remove the cause, remove the effect.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Conditional doctrines die with their conditions.
Both terms are load-bearing, neither decorative.
Moods pass; structures persist while fed.
Test concepts by removing each pillar.
Share this: imagine one longing fully answered.

puzzles.title: The Quantity Ethic
puzzles.question: Don Juan's endless loves exemplify Camus's ethic of quantity — living the most experiences possible rather than the deepest single one.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. With no ultimate hierarchy of lives, Don Juan multiplies experience: quantity becomes the absurd ethic. Each love lived fully, none mistaken for eternity.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Don Juan doesn't love deeply once but completely each time — the ethic of quantity over illusory depth. Where eternity is unavailable, multiplicity is honesty.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Multiplicity can be honesty where eternity is closed.
Quantity becomes ethic when hierarchies collapse.
Each fully, none forever: the Don Juan rule.
Depth-illusions waste what breadth could live.
Share this: multiply one experience this month.

puzzles.title: The Many Lives
puzzles.question: Camus's actor lives absurdly well by dying many stage deaths — sampling countless lives within one brief span.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The actor compresses centuries into evenings, living and dying on schedule. Brief time, maximum lives: quantity's theatrical form.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Where Don Juan multiplies loves, the actor multiplies selves — Hamlet tonight, Lear tomorrow. One lifespan, countless traversals: the absurd arithmetic of the stage.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Selves can multiply like loves and days.
Stages compress centuries into evenings.
Traversal beats duration in absurd arithmetic.
Sample widely within narrow spans.

puzzles.title: The Day's Master
puzzles.question: The conqueror — Camus's man of action — masters his days by choosing fully within limits, demanding everything from the present hour.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Conquerors act without appeal to tomorrow: efficiency, adventure, chosen struggle. Mastery of hours replaces mastery of history.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The conqueror knows victories fade and acts anyway — present-tense fullness over future-tense salvation. Days, not destinies, are the conquerable territory.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hours are conquerable where histories are not.
Present-tense fullness beats future-tense salvation.
Act without appeal to tomorrow's ledger.
Choose fully inside acknowledged limits.

puzzles.title: The Licensed Blade
puzzles.question: Because revolt rejects all limits, Camus permits revolutionary violence without restraint in the name of freedom.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. The Rebel draws the line: revolt says no to oppression, including the rebel's own slide into executioner. 'Neither victim nor executioner' bounds every blade.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Camus's rebel refuses murder's logic even for liberation — unlimited violence repeats the tyranny it claims to fight. Limits are revolt's spine, not its betrayal.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Rebellions must refuse their own tyrannies.
Means infect ends; blades cut both ways.
Bounded revolt outlasts absolute license.
Check every liberation for new executioners.

puzzles.title: The Twin Refusal
puzzles.question: 'Neither victim nor executioner' compresses Camus's rebel ethic: refuse suffering oppression and refuse inflicting it.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The twin refusal draws revolt's clean line: resist the executioner without becoming one. Symmetry of refusal is the whole morality.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Victimhood accepted breeds complicity; executionerhood seized breeds tyranny. The rebel's narrow path threads between — refusing both chairs at the violent table.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Twin refusals draw cleaner lines than single ones.
Resist without replicating the violence.
Narrow paths thread between two chairs.
Symmetry of refusal is complete morality.

puzzles.title: The Open License
puzzles.question: Camus's absurd implies that, with no ultimate values, literally everything is permitted and no act can be condemned.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Camus explicitly denies the license: revolt founds values — human solidarity, limits, refusal of murder. Absence of absolutes is not absence of ethics.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'Everything is permitted' is the slogan Camus refutes, not preaches: revolt generates its own limits from shared confrontation. Ethics without absolutes still condemns the executioner.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Absence of absolutes never equals absence of ethics.
Shared confrontation founds shared limits.
Refuted slogans get misattributed constantly.
Read what follows the famous premises.

puzzles.title: The Owned Hour
puzzles.question: For the absurd man, the present moment is the only secure possession — neither past nor future can be owned, so full presence is the demand.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Hope mortgages presence to futures that never pay; nostalgia spends it backward. Only the hour in hand is ownable — live it entirely.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Past is uneditable, future unwritten; presence alone is property. Camus's temporal ethic concentrates all wealth into now — spend it completely or lose it doubly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Presence alone is ownable property.
Hope mortgages hours to nonpaying futures.
Nostalgia spends wealth backward.
Concentrate riches into the hour in hand.

puzzles.title: The Afterlife Exit
puzzles.question: Hoping for an afterlife that redeems suffering counts, for Camus, as another escape from the absurd rather than an answer to it.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Deferred justice dissolves the confrontation by promising reconciliation — philosophical suicide in eschatological dress. Revolt wants no settlement, here or hereafter.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Afterlife hope trades present lucidity for future compensation, exiting the tension Camus demands we keep. Settlement refused is the doctrine's spine — no deals, temporal or eternal.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Deferred settlements exit present tensions.
Compensation promises dissolve confrontations.
No-deals policies span time and eternity.
Keep the tension; refuse the settlement.

puzzles.title: The Hoping Stone
puzzles.question: Sisyphus should hope that this time the rock stays balanced at the summit, since hope would lighten his eternal task.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Hope betrays lucidity — it mortgages the present to a future the gods control. Sisyphus owns only the push; hoping outsources his happiness to the summit.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Hope would convert revolt into waiting, surrendering the owned hour to unowned outcomes. The myth's ethic forbids exactly this comfort: no hope, full living.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hope can betray lucidity it claims to serve.
Mortgaged presents enrich no one.
Owned pushes beat outsourced summits.
Comforts that surrender stance are traps.
Share this: push one rock hopelessly and happily.

puzzles.title: The Cold Proof
puzzles.question: Camus derives the absurd through strict logical deduction from self-evident first principles, like a geometer proving theorems.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. He begins from a feeling — the encounter with strangeness, nausea at routine — and reasons outward. Absurd reasoning starts in experience, not axioms.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The Myth opens with weariness, disgust, the weight of days: phenomenology first, logic after. Geometers deduce; Camus describes, then follows the description where it leads.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Feelings can found philosophies legitimately.
Description precedes deduction in lived thought.
Axioms miss what encounters reveal.
Start from nausea, not from nothing.
Share this: describe one strange Tuesday fully.

puzzles.title: The World Alone
puzzles.question: A universe empty of all conscious beings would still contain the absurd as a property of silent matter itself.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. No questioners, no confrontation, no absurd — silent matter alone is merely silent. The concept needs its human term absolutely.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Absurdity is relational: remove minds and only muteness remains, unopposed and unabsurd. Properties of encounters vanish with either party.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Relational properties need both relata present.
Encounters vanish with either party gone.
Muteness alone is not absurdity.
Test attributions by subtraction.
Share this: subtract minds from one landscape.

puzzles.title: The Mind Alone
puzzles.question: Human longing by itself — even in a world that answered every question — would still generate the absurd from within.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Satisfied longing is not absurd; the concept requires the world's refusal. Longing alone is just appetite — tragedy needs the locked door.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Appetite without obstacle is merely hunger, fed or feedable. The absurd is the locked door experienced by the hungry — remove the lock and only appetite remains.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Appetites need obstacles to become tragic.
Locked doors complete hunger's drama.
Satisfaction dissolves what refusal creates.
Single terms never make relations.
Share this: find one hunger with no lock.

puzzles.title: The Worst Labor
puzzles.question: Camus opens by calling Sisyphus's fate horrible: the gods designed futile, hopeless labor as the ultimate punishment.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The opening grants the horror fully — futile endless toil as the gods' worst invention. Only then does revolt invert it; the happiness lands because the horror was conceded.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Camus never minimizes: 'the horrible punishment' stands unsoftened. Concession precedes inversion — happiness means something only against admitted horror.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Concede horror before inverting it.
Unsoftened premises make real conclusions.
Inversion needs weight to work against.
Never minimize what you mean to transcend.
Share this: admit one horror fully today.

puzzles.title: The Lucid Wound
puzzles.question: Sisyphus's consciousness of his fate is simultaneously his tragedy and his victory — it makes the torment real and makes revolt possible.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Unconscious rolling would be mere mechanics; lucid rolling is tragedy owned — and ownership is victory. Consciousness wounds and crowns at once.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The rock crushes, but awareness converts crushing into confrontation: tragedy admitted becomes triumph chosen. One faculty, two edges — the wound that is also the crown.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Awareness wounds and crowns together.
Owned tragedy converts to chosen triumph.
Mechanics become meaning through lucidity.
Single faculties cut both ways.
Share this: own one torment consciously.

puzzles.title: The Just Gods
puzzles.question: Oedipus concludes that the gods treated him justly, and Camus endorses this theodicy as the myth's true moral.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Oedipus concludes 'all is well' — fate become his own matter — not that gods were fair. Camus endorses lucid ownership, never divine justice.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The essay's Oedipus finds everything his own, not everything just: 'all is well' means fate internalized, not gods vindicated. Theodicy is another consolation revolt refuses.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Ownership differs from vindication entirely.
'All is well' internalizes; it never absolves.
Theodicy is consolation in disguise.
Read conclusions for what they actually claim.
Share this: own one fate without justifying it.

puzzles.title: The Unconsoled
puzzles.question: Camusian revolt permanently refuses consolation — no hope, no faith, no future settlement may soften the lucid confrontation.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Consolation dissolves tension, and tension is the required state. The unconsoled stance holds through every offered comfort.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Hopes, faiths, and settlements all exit through the same door: they end the confrontation revolt must maintain. Refusal is permanent because the condition is.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Comforts that end tension are exits.
Permanence matches the permanent condition.
Refusal maintained is revolt defined.
Softening is surrender spelled kindly.
Share this: refuse one softening today.

puzzles.title: The Empty Detachment
puzzles.question: Meursault's emotional detachment proves that, for Camus, nothing matters at all — not sun, sea, friendship, or sensory joy.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Meursault loves swimming, sunlight, Marie — his honesty is about feeling truly, not feeling nothing. Detachment from lies, attachment to senses.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The Stranger's crime is refusing comforting falsehoods, not lacking love: sun, sea, and Marie fill him genuinely. Honesty about feeling differs totally from absence of it.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Honesty about feeling differs from feeling nothing.
Refusing lies is not refusing life.
Senses fill whom sermons leave empty.
Read detachment for its actual object.
Share this: love one sunlight honestly.

puzzles.title: The Limitless Emperor
puzzles.question: Caligula's murders and defiance show that absurd freedom recognizes no limits whatsoever — the logical endpoint Camus celebrates.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Caligula is the cautionary inversion: freedom pushed past revolt's limits destroys what revolt protects. Camus stages the endpoint to condemn it.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The play exhibits absurd logic weaponized — and self-devouring. Endpoints that eat their own foundations warn; revolt's limits (no murder) are the lesson Caligula's corpse teaches.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Endpoints that devour foundations warn, not beckon.
Weaponized logic self-destructs on schedule.
Limits protect revolt from its own emperors.
Stage extremes to condemn them.
Share this: spot one freedom eating itself.

puzzles.title: The Barbara Chain
puzzles.question: All mammals are warm-blooded. All whales are mammals. Therefore, all whales are warm-blooded. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Barbara's chain links cleanly: whales sit inside mammals, mammals inside warm-blooded, so whales land inside warm-blooded. Valid form, true premises.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. All S are M plus all M are P guarantees all S are P — the terms nest like bowls. Validity here is structural; truth of premises makes it sound too.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Nesting terms guarantee nesting conclusions.
All-S-are-M plus all-M-are-P always yields all-S-are-P.
Bowls-inside-bowls picture every Barbara.
Form validity plus true premises equals soundness.
Share this: build one Barbara about your kitchen.

puzzles.title: The Backward Proof
puzzles.question: If it rains, the streets get wet. The streets are wet. Therefore, it rained. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Wet streets have many causes — cleaners, burst pipes, sprinklers. Affirming the consequent mistakes one sufficient condition for the only one.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'If rain then wet' plus 'wet' never yields 'rain': consequences outnumber their causes. Affirming the consequent is the most committed fallacy in daily reasoning.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Consequences outnumber their causes always.
Sufficient is not necessary — rain suffices, others too.
Backward proofs need ruling out rivals.
'If P then Q; Q' stops exactly there.
Share this: name three causes of one wet street.

puzzles.title: The Dry Denial
puzzles.question: If the oven reaches full heat, the bread browns. The oven never heated. Therefore, the bread stayed pale. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Denying the antecedent forgets rival browners — broilers, blowtorches, yesterday's bake. No heat removes one cause, not all.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'If heat then brown' plus 'no heat' leaves every other browning method standing. Pale needs ruling out all causes, and the argument rules out one.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Removing one cause removes only one cause.
Broilers and torches survive every oven denial.
Pale conclusions need all causes excluded.
Antecedents deny; consequents stay standing.
Share this: brown one bread without any oven.

puzzles.title: The Forward Step
puzzles.question: If the alarm rings, classes empty. The alarm rings. Therefore, classes empty. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Modus ponens: the trigger fired, so the guaranteed result follows. Forward steps from true conditionals never misfire.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'If P then Q' plus 'P' delivers Q by the simplest valid move in logic. Ponens affirms forward; only backward moves (affirming Q) break.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Triggers fired deliver guaranteed results.
Forward moves from true conditionals never misfire.
Ponens is logic's simplest valid step.
Affirm the antecedent; collect the consequent.
Share this: fire one modus ponens aloud today.

puzzles.title: The Full Hallway
puzzles.question: If the fuel ignites, the rocket lifts. The rocket sits on the pad. Therefore, the fuel never ignited. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Modus tollens: the guaranteed result absent means the trigger never fired. Grounded rockets testify against ignition.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'If ignition then liftoff' plus 'no liftoff' kills ignition — the result's absence testifies against its trigger. Pads hold rockets whose fuel slept.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Grounded rockets testify against ignition.
Absent results eliminate their triggers.
Tollens takes away what ponens would give.
'No liftoff' is evidence about fuel, full stop.
Share this: ground one excuse with tollens today.

puzzles.title: The Shared Circle
puzzles.question: All violins are instruments. All trumpets are instruments. Therefore, all violins are trumpets. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Sharing the orchestra never merges the sections. The middle term must connect extremes, not merely room with both.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'Instruments' sits undistributed in both premises — it never speaks about all instruments, so violins and trumpets float unlinked inside it. Shared stages prove nothing about players.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Shared stages never merge the sections.
Middle terms must connect, not cohabit.
Undistributed middles float conclusions loose.
Link extremes through the middle, never beside it.
Share this: seat violins and trumpets inside instruments.

puzzles.title: The Empty Net
puzzles.question: No stars are planets. All suns are stars. Therefore, no suns are planets. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Celarent excludes cleanly: suns sit inside stars, stars wholly outside planets, so suns land outside too. Negative universals chain like positives.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'No M are P' plus 'all S are M' fences S outside P without exception. Exclusion inherits downward exactly as inclusion does.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Exclusion inherits downward like inclusion.
Fences around big groups pen all subgroups.
Negative universals chain as cleanly as positives.
Outside-outside reasoning needs no extra rule.
Share this: fence one sun outside today.

puzzles.title: The Partial Net
puzzles.question: All birds have feathers. Some pets are birds. Therefore, some pets have feathers. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Darii carries the universal down to the partial case: the pet-birds inherit feathers with their birdhood. Some-premises yield some-conclusions legitimately.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'All M are P' plus 'some S are M' places those S inside P — the some-quantifier survives the trip. Partial premises license partial conclusions, never wholes.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Universals descend safely onto partial cases.
Some-premises license some-conclusions only.
Pet-birds inherit with their birdhood intact.
Never inflate 'some' conclusions into 'all'.
Share this: land one universal on a partial pet.

puzzles.title: The Partial Fence
puzzles.question: No fish breathe air. Some swimmers are fish. Therefore, some swimmers do not breathe air. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Ferio fences the partial case out: the swimmer-fish inherit airlessness with their fishhood. Negative universals govern some-cases too.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'No M are P' plus 'some S are M' excludes those S from P — the fence covers subgroups partially present. Exclusion reaches the some-quantifier intact.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Fences cover partial subgroups too.
Negative universals govern some-cases fully.
Excluded middles exclude their members.
Some-not conclusions are perfectly respectable.
Share this: fence one swimmer out today.

puzzles.title: The Bank Switch
puzzles.question: All banks hold money. River banks are banks. Therefore, river banks hold money. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. 'Bank' shifts meaning mid-argument — financial versus riverside — making four terms, not three. Equivocation smuggles a second middle term aboard.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Valid syllogisms need exactly three terms used consistently; 'bank' plays two roles, so the middle never connects. Same spelling is not same meaning — check term identity.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Same spelling is never same meaning guaranteed.
Three terms means three, used consistently.
Equivocation smuggles extra middles aboard.
Check identity before chaining words.
Share this: catch one equivocation in the wild.

puzzles.title: The Double Negative
puzzles.question: No sailors are pilots. No captains are sailors. Therefore, no captains are pilots. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Two negative premises never yield a conclusion — they exclude without connecting. Negatives fence apart; they cannot bridge.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'No A are B' plus 'no C are B' leaves A and C unlinked: both outside B, relation between them unknown. Exclusion without connection concludes nothing.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Two negatives conclude nothing, ever.
Fences apart never bridge together.
Exclusion needs one inclusion to conclude.
Count the negatives before trusting chains.
Share this: build one double-negative dead end.

puzzles.title: The Horned Proof
puzzles.question: All unicorns have exactly one horn. Therefore, some existing creature has exactly one horn. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Universal claims about unicorns say nothing about existence — 'all' can hold vacuously over an empty set. Existence is never a free conclusion.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'All unicorns' quantifies over zero actual beasts; universals hold vacuously without members. Modern logic demands existential import be earned, never assumed.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Universals hold vacuously over empty sets.
Existence is never a free conclusion.
'All' describes members; it never creates them.
Earn existential import separately.
Share this: prove nothing exists from an 'all'.

puzzles.title: The Flipped All
puzzles.question: All squares are rectangles. Therefore, all rectangles are squares. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Conversion fails for A-propositions: inclusion runs one way. Squares nest inside rectangles; rectangles sprawl far beyond squares.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'All A are B' never converts to 'all B are A' — nesting is directional. Long rectangles refute the flip instantly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Inclusion runs one direction only.
Nesting never reverses by conversion.
A-propositions convert illicitly, always.
Check direction before flipping quantifiers.
Share this: flip one inclusion and watch it break.

puzzles.title: The Flipped None
puzzles.question: No goalkeepers are strikers. Therefore, no strikers are goalkeepers. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. E-propositions convert cleanly: mutual exclusion is symmetric. No-overlap reads identically both directions.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'No A are B' and 'no B are A' say one symmetric thing: the positions never overlap. Exclusion, unlike inclusion, reverses safely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Exclusion is symmetric; inclusion is not.
No-overlap reads identically both ways.
E-propositions convert freely, always.
Symmetry belongs to fences, never nests.
Share this: flip one exclusion safely today.

puzzles.title: The Flipped Some
puzzles.question: Some students are athletes. Therefore, some athletes are students. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. I-propositions convert: overlap is symmetric. The shared members witness both directions at once.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'Some A are B' names overlapping members who are simultaneously B-that-are-A. Overlap, like exclusion, reverses without loss.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Overlap reverses without any loss.
Shared members witness both directions.
I-propositions convert as freely as E ones.
Symmetry covers fences and overlaps alike.
Share this: flip one overlap today.

puzzles.title: The Long Chain
puzzles.question: All A are B. All B are C. All C are D. Therefore, all A are D. This extended chain is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Sorites chains link Barbara repeatedly: nesting is transitive across any length. Bowls within bowls within bowls.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Each link is a valid Barbara, and validity composes: A⊆B⊆C⊆D yields A⊆D directly. Chains hold however long the nesting runs.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Validity composes across any chain length.
Nesting is transitive without exception.
Each link checked makes the chain trustworthy.
Long sorites are repeated Barbaras.
Share this: build one four-link nesting chain.

puzzles.title: The Mortal Socrates
puzzles.question: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Therefore, Socrates is mortal. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The textbook Barbara: Socrates sits inside men, men inside mortals, so Socrates lands inside mortals. Two millennia of agreement.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Singular premises ('Socrates is a man') function as universals about one member. Nest the individual, inherit the predicate — philosophy's most famous valid move.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Individuals nest like classes with one member.
Singular premises behave universally.
Inherit predicates through membership.
Famous forms earned fame by never failing.
Share this: syllogize one famous individual.

puzzles.title: The Mortal Confusion
puzzles.question: All soufflés are egg dishes. This omelette is an egg dish. Therefore, this omelette is a soufflé. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Egg dishes include frittatas, quiches, and omelettes — the omelette's membership proves nothing about souffléhood. Affirming the predicate proves nothing about the subject.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'All soufflés are egg dishes' plus 'omelette is an egg dish' is affirming the consequent in whites: egghood has countless sources. Shared predicates never identify subjects.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Shared predicates never identify subjects.
Egghood has countless non-soufflé sources.
Consequent affirmed proves nothing backward.
Aprons don't rescue bad forms.
Share this: egg one non-soufflé memorably.

puzzles.title: The Dry Streets
puzzles.question: If frost comes, the basil dies. The basil thrives. Therefore, no frost came. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Thriving basil denies the guaranteed result, so the trigger never fired — textbook tollens. Absence of wilt testifies against frost.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'If frost then death' plus 'thriving' eliminates frost: results absent mean triggers absent. Denying the consequent is the safe backward move.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Thriving testifies against frost directly.
Absent results eliminate their triggers.
Consequent denied denies antecedents safely.
Backward-safe moves mirror forward ones.
Share this: tollens one green garden today.

puzzles.title: The Either Or
puzzles.question: The alarm means fire or drill. It is not a drill. Therefore, it is a fire. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Disjunctive syllogism: eliminating one alternative leaves the other standing. Either-or plus not-one yields the other.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'P or Q' plus 'not P' delivers Q — elimination is deduction. Alternatives exhausted leave survivors standing.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Elimination is deduction in disguise.
Exhausted alternatives leave survivors.
Either-or plus not-one yields the other.
Disjoin, deny, collect the remainder.
Share this: eliminate one alternative to conclude.

puzzles.title: The Inclusive Trap
puzzles.question: The pass covers bus or tram (or both). She rode the bus. Therefore, she did not ride the tram. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Inclusive 'or' tolerates both — bus-plus-tram days exist. Affirming one alternative never denies the other.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'Or' in logic includes 'both' unless stated otherwise; affirming the bus leaves the tram entirely open. Both-together commutes break every exclusive reading.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Logical 'or' includes 'both' by default.
Affirming one alternative denies nothing.
Both-together commutes break exclusive readings.
Check inclusivity before eliminating.
Share this: find one both-together commute.

puzzles.title: The If Chain
puzzles.question: If you study, you pass. If you pass, you graduate. Therefore, if you study, you graduate. This chain is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Hypothetical syllogism links conditionals transitively: study routes through passing to graduating. If-chains compose like nesting.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. P→Q plus Q→R yields P→R — the middle consequent-antecedent cancels like middle terms. Conditional chains hold across any length.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Conditionals compose transitively, always.
Middle links cancel like middle terms.
If-chains are Barbaras in disguise.
Link study to graduation stepwise.
Share this: chain two of today's conditionals.

puzzles.title: The Pet Exclusion
puzzles.question: No sharks are whales. Some hunters are sharks. Therefore, some hunters are not whales. This argument is valid.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Ferio again in fins: the hunter-sharks inherit non-whaleness with their sharkhood. Partial premises, partial exclusions, full validity.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'No S are W' plus 'some H are S' fences those hunters outside whaleness. The some-quantifier carries exclusion faithfully to its members.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hunter-sharks inherit non-whaleness automatically.
Partial premises carry full exclusions.
Ferio wears fins without losing form.
Some-not conclusions close real arguments.
Share this: Ferio one ocean hunter today.

puzzles.title: The Reverse Rule
puzzles.question: A valid argument can have false premises and a false conclusion at the same time.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Validity is form only: 'All fish fly; Nemo is a fish; so Nemo flies' is perfectly valid with every claim false. Form and truth travel separately.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Validity checks structure, never content — false premises can validly entail false conclusions. Soundness adds truth; validity alone promises only conditional safety.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Form and truth travel separately always.
False premises can validly entail falsehoods.
Validity promises conditional safety only.
Soundness is validity plus truth.
Share this: validate one all-false argument.

puzzles.title: The True Guarantee
puzzles.question: A valid argument with true premises must always have a true conclusion.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. That guarantee defines deductive validity: true premises cannot validly lead astray. Soundness seals truth from assumptions to conclusion.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Validity means impossibility of true-premises-plus-false-conclusion — that is the entire definition. Trust the seal: sound arguments never betray.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Impossibility of true-to-false defines validity.
Seals hold from assumptions to conclusions.
Sound arguments never betray their premises.
Trust the guarantee; check the premises.
Share this: seal one argument sound today.

puzzles.title: The Leaked Secret
puzzles.question: Interference dies exactly when the environment could tell which path was taken — even if nobody reads the record. What leaks out and kills the fringes?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Which-path information — leakage, not disturbance, ends superposition. Knowability anywhere collapses coherence everywhere.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is which-path information. Gentle uninformative kicks preserve fringes; informative whispers destroy them. Environments measure by gossiping, and gossip is fatal to coherence.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Leakage, not force, ends quantum coherence.
Knowability anywhere collapses superpositions everywhere.
Environments measure continuously by gossiping.
Seal information channels to preserve fringes.
Share this: name one leak that ruins one secret.

puzzles.title: The Survivor States
puzzles.question: Most superpositions die on contact with air, yet a few special states shrug off monitoring and persist. What are these robust states called?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Pointer states — the environment's monitoring singles out survivors that don't entangle further. Classicality is selective survival, not universal law.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is pointer states. While fragile superpositions decohere instantly, states that commute with the interaction persist — the environment elects them by failing to disturb them. Survival defines classicality.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Monitoring elects survivors by failing to disturb them.
Robustness under watching defines classical states.
Fragile alternatives decohere into oblivion fast.
Selection, not law, builds the classical world.
Share this: name one survivor of constant scrutiny.

puzzles.title: The Selector
puzzles.question: Environment-induced superselection explains why some states become classical. Which physicist's principle names this selection?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Zurek — einselection (environment-induced superselection) is his framework for classical emergence. Monitoring selects; selection explains.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is Zurek. Wojciech Zurek's einselection shows preferred states emerging from interaction Hamiltonians, not postulates. The environment votes, and its votes are the classical world.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Frameworks beat postulates for explaining emergence.
Interaction Hamiltonians cast the deciding votes.
Selection principles replace collapse axioms.
Follow the votes, not the wishes.
Share this: credit one selector behind one classical fact.

puzzles.title: The Instant Classical
puzzles.question: A floating dust grain in daylight loses all quantum coherence many orders of magnitude faster than any measurement could catch. On human timescales, how fast is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Instantly — ~10⁻³¹ seconds estimated, incomprehensibly below any clock. Daylight classicalizes dust before physics begins.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Close — the answer is instantly. Air collisions plus sunlight scatter which-path data at rates no instrument follows. Dust never had a quantum moment in any operational sense.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Daylight classicalizes dust before physics begins.
Scattering rates defeat every instrument built.
Operationally, some coherences never existed.
Timescales decide what counts as real.
Share this: imagine 10⁻³¹ seconds honestly failing.

puzzles.title: The Faded Matrix
puzzles.question: Decoherence zeroes the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix while preserving the diagonals. What does the state become?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Diagonal — off-diagonals (coherences) decay, leaving classical probabilities on the diagonal. Interference dies; ignorance remains.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is diagonal. The density matrix keeps its populations while its coherences evaporate — a mixture wearing a superposition's clothes. Diagonal means decided-but-unknown, not indefinite.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Off-diagonals carry coherence; diagonals carry odds.
Decay of the former is decoherence defined.
Mixtures wear superpositions' discarded clothes.
Read matrices for what evaporated.
Share this: zero one off-diagonal on paper.

puzzles.title: The Copied World
puzzles.question: Quantum Darwinism says objectivity arises because the environment proliferates many copies of selected information. What spreads everywhere?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Redundancy — countless environment fragments independently carry the same data, so observers agree without disturbing anything. Objectivity is overwhelming consensus of copies.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is redundancy. One photon tells little; 10²⁰ agreeing photons make facts. Reality feels solid because its records are redundantly broadcast, not because anything collapsed.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Consensus of copies builds felt solidity.
Single records persuade nobody; avalanches convince.
Objectivity is broadcast density, not magic.
Count the copies behind every fact.
Share this: intercept one fact from two photons.

puzzles.title: The Agreed Reality
puzzles.question: Independent observers examining different environment fragments always agree on pointer-state outcomes. What does redundancy manufacture?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Objective reality — agreement across independent fragments without prior coordination. Shared access to redundant records is what 'out there' means.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is objective reality. Each observer samples different photons yet reports identical outcomes — coordination-free consensus. 'Out there' cashes out as redundantly accessible information.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Agreement without coordination defines objectivity.
Independent samples converging means shared facts.
'Out there' is accessibility, not essence.
Redundant access manufactures common worlds.
Share this: agree with a stranger via photons.

puzzles.title: The Immune Corner
puzzles.question: Certain symmetric multi-qubit states never entangle with collective noise and so never decohere. What are these protected corners called?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Decoherence-free subspaces — symmetries the noise cannot see, so coherence hides in plain sight. Identical coupling leaves relative phases untouched.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is decoherence-free subspaces. When noise strikes all qubits identically, antisymmetric combinations stay invisible to it. Hide in symmetry what the environment cannot distinguish.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Symmetries hide what noise cannot distinguish.
Identical coupling spares relative phases.
Protected corners exploit the enemy's blindness.
Invisibility beats shielding for fragile states.
Share this: hide one secret in plain symmetry.

puzzles.title: The Refocused Spin
puzzles.question: A clever pulse sequence reverses slow dephasing, making decayed signals briefly revive. What technique refocuses the spins?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Spin echoes — a π-pulse time-reverses inhomogeneous precession, refocusing what spread. Reversible dephasing is inhomogeneity, not true loss.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is spin echoes. Hahn's pulses flip the runners so laggards lead: static spreads rewind, true decoherence doesn't. Echoes separate reversible blur from irreversible loss.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Time-reversal pulses rewind static spreads.
Runners flipped make laggards lead briefly.
Revival distinguishes blur from true loss.
Inhomogeneity rewinds; leakage never does.
Share this: flip one race halfway and watch.

puzzles.title: The Energy Clock
puzzles.question: Qubit engineers track two lifetimes: one for energy leaking to the environment, one for phase scrambling. What does the energy lifetime measure?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Energy relaxation (T1) — excited populations decaying to ground by emission. Energy lost is information thermalized.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is energy relaxation. T1 clocks populations falling, distinct from phases scrambling (T2). Emission events are irreversible donations to the bath.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Populations fall while phases scramble separately.
Emission donates energy irreversibly to baths.
Two clocks track two distinct deaths.
Relaxation thermalizes what dephasing merely blurs.
Share this: time one excited state falling.

puzzles.title: The Phase Clock
puzzles.question: Beyond energy loss, qubits suffer pure phase randomization with no energy exchange. What does this faster, subtler decay quantify?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Dephasing — phase randomization without energy cost, the silent killer of superpositions. No emission, no trace, just blur.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is dephasing. Elastic fluctuations jitter phases while populations stand — coherence dies with energy books balanced. The subtler death usually wins the race.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Phases randomize without spending energy.
Silent killers outrun noisy ones typically.
Blur without loss is decoherence's specialty.
Track phases separately from populations.
Share this: jitter one clock without moving hands.

puzzles.title: The Low Rumble
puzzles.question: Superconducting qubits are haunted by noise growing stronger at low frequencies, defying simple white-noise models. What spectrum dominates?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 1/f noise — flicker from charge traps and flux wanderers, rising as frequency falls. Slow drifts dominate solid-state dephasing.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 1/f noise. White models predict flat spectra; real devices rumble louder the slower you listen. Material defects conduct this bass line of decoherence.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Slow drifts dominate solid-state coherence loss.
Flat-spectrum models fail real devices.
Material defects conduct decoherence's bass line.
Listen low to find the true enemy.
Share this: hear one flicker beneath one hum.

puzzles.title: The Error Promise
puzzles.question: A foundational result guarantees arbitrarily long quantum computation provided physical error rates sit below a critical value. What result promises this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The threshold theorem — below ~1% (surface codes), concatenated correction suppresses logical errors exponentially. Imperfect parts, perfect wholes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is threshold theorem. It converts hardware quality into a yes-no: beat the threshold and scaling works, miss it and correction drowns. Fault tolerance is a phase transition in error space.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Quality thresholds decide scalability binarily.
Exponential suppression Smiths sub-threshold errors.
Imperfect parts compose into perfect wholes.
Phase transitions hide in error rates.
Share this: name one threshold that changes everything.

puzzles.title: The Tiled Defense
puzzles.question: One error-correction architecture tiles qubits on a 2D grid, tolerating the highest physical error rates known (~1%). Which code?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Surface code — topological protection on a tile grid, with the kindest thresholds in the business. Local checks, global memory.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is surface code. Tiling stabilizers across a lattice detects errors locally while storing logically globally. Topology guards what geometry exposes.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Local checks can guard global memory.
Topology protects what geometry exposes.
Grids beat concatenations for real thresholds.
Tile defenses scale where others stall.
Share this: tile one defense on graph paper.

puzzles.title: The Quiet Observer
puzzles.question: In Quantum Darwinism the environment is not a destroyer but an observer, redundantly recording systems for all to see. What role does it play?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Witness — the environment observes, records, and broadcasts, manufacturing objectivity. Destroyer is the old job title; witness is the promotion.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is witness. Same photons that decohere also testify: monitoring that kills coherence births consensus. Reframe the environment from vandal to court reporter.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Monitors that kill coherence birth consensus.
Vandals reframe as court reporters here.
Testimony requires redundant recording.
Witnesses manufacture shared facts.
Share this: thank one photon for testifying.

puzzles.title: The Spread Record
puzzles.question: No-cloning forbids copying quantum states, yet environments end up full of system records. What proliferates without violating the ban?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Classical records — decoherence converts quantum information into classical imprints, which copy freely. The ban covers quanta; records are classical.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is classical records. No-cloning guards superpositions, not pointer-state outcomes: once decohered, information is classical and proliferates legally. Conversion precedes proliferation.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Conversion precedes legal proliferation.
Bans cover quanta, never classical outcomes.
Pointer data copies where qubits cannot.
Decohere first, broadcast second.
Share this: copy one classical record freely.

puzzles.title: The Returning Tide
puzzles.question: In structured environments, lost coherence sometimes flows back, reviving dead superpositions temporarily. What returns from the bath?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Information — non-Markovian backflow returns what Markovian baths keep. Memory in the environment means death isn't final.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is information. Structured baths remember and refund: revivals testify that leakage went to memory, not oblivion. Backflow distinguishes baths with history.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Baths with memory refund leaked coherence.
Revivals testify to history, not miracles.
Backflow distinguishes structured environments.
Death isn't final where memory persists.
Share this: welcome one refunded coherence.

puzzles.title: The Forgetful Bath
puzzles.question: Simple decoherence models assume the environment forgets instantly, with no memory of past interactions. What approximation is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Markov approximation — memoryless baths simplify dynamics to one-way leakage. Convenient, often true, sometimes catastrophically false.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is Markov approximation. Forgetting instantly means no revivals, no backflow, clean exponentials. Structured environments break the promise and remember.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Forgetting simplifies dynamics enormously.
Memoryless baths leak one way only.
Convenient approximations fail structurally sometimes.
Check memory before assuming Markov.
Share this: forgive one bath its memory.

puzzles.title: The Oscillator Sea
puzzles.question: A canonical model couples a quantum system to an infinite bath of harmonic oscillators with ohmic damping. Which model?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Caldeira-Leggett — the oscillator sea that made macroscopic quantum tunneling calculable. Infinite springs model every friction.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is Caldeira-Leggett. Ohmic baths of oscillators reproduce dissipation from first principles, grounding decoherence rates in spectral densities. Seas of springs explain friction quantumly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Infinite springs model every friction.
Spectral densities ground decoherence rates.
Canonical baths make tunneling calculable.
Ohmic seas explain everyday dissipation.
Share this: swim one oscillator sea mentally.

puzzles.title: The Fitness Filter
puzzles.question: Zurek's sieve ranks quantum states by how predictably they survive environmental monitoring. What filter predicts classicality?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Predictability sieve — states producing the least entropy under monitoring win classicality. Fitness means forecastability here.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is predictability sieve. Rank states by entropy generated during monitoring; the quietest survive as classical. Darwinism needs a fitness function, and predictability is it.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Fitness means forecastability under monitoring.
Quietest states survive environmental scrutiny.
Sieves rank candidates before selecting.
Entropy production measures unfitness.
Share this: sieve one habit by predictability.

puzzles.title: The Position Habit
puzzles.question: Interactions in nature depend on distance, so environments monitor location relentlessly. Why is position the preferred basis?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Local interactions — forces act here, not in superposition-space, so position gets monitored and selected. Habitats of interaction choose the basis.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is local interactions. Hamiltonians couple nearby things, so environments resolve where, not exotic superpositions of where. Basis preference is interaction geography.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Geography of interaction chooses bases.
Nearby couplings monitor locations relentlessly.
Habitats decide what gets selected.
Position wins by being what forces touch.
Share this: touch one reason for position.

puzzles.title: The Missing Outcome
puzzles.question: Decoherence explains why interference vanishes, but one mystery remains: why this outcome rather than that one. What does it not explain?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Definite outcomes — decoherence yields and-or mixtures, never this-not-that actuality. The measurement problem survives, narrowed but alive.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is definite outcomes. Vanished interference explains unobservability of superpositions, not selection among alternatives. Honest decoherence admits its boundary; interpretations fight over the remainder.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Vanished fringes never select alternatives.
And-or mixtures differ from this-not-that.
Honest theories admit their boundaries.
Remainders belong to interpretations.
Share this: ask why this outcome, not that.

puzzles.title: The Split World
puzzles.question: In Everettian language, decoherence marks where one quantum state differentiates into non-interfering histories. What forms?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Branches — decohered histories that never re-interfere, each internally classical. Splitting is leakage made ontological.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is branches. Where Copenhagen says collapse, Everett says differentiation: non-interfering histories each host observers. Decoherence draws the branch lines.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Differentiation draws lines collapse only names.
Non-interfering histories host separate observers.
Splitting is leakage made ontological.
Branch lines follow decoherence fronts.
Share this: stand on one branch and wave.

puzzles.title: The Airy Eraser
puzzles.question: Matter-wave fringes vanish in poor vacuum because gas molecules scatter off the travelers, recording paths. What kills the pattern?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Collisions — each scattered molecule carries away path data. Vacuum quality is fringe quality, directly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is collisions. Gas scattering entangles traveler with air, broadcasting which-path records at every impact. Pump down to cohere; vent to classicalize.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Vacuum quality equals fringe quality directly.
Impacts broadcast path records instantly.
Pump down to cohere, vent to classicalize.
Air is a relentless which-path detector.
Share this: blame one collision for classicality.

puzzles.title: The Glowing Betrayal
puzzles.question: Hot fullerenes emit infrared photons that reveal their paths, washing out interference that cold ones show. What betrays them?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Thermal radiation — self-emitted photons carry which-path data to infinity. Hot objects confess their trajectories by glowing.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is thermal radiation. Internal heat becomes external information: every emitted photon is a path record escaping forever. Cool to cohere; glow to go classical.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Self-glow confesses trajectories publicly.
Heat converts to information irreversibly.
Escaping photons are permanent records.
Cool to cohere; glow to go classical.
Share this: dim one glow to save one fringe.

puzzles.title: The False Net
puzzles.question: Four paper shapes: a cross of five squares plus one attached to an arm; a staircase of two offset rows of three; a row of four with one square above the second and one below the third; a solid 2×3 rectangle. Which CANNOT fold into a closed cube?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The 2×3 rectangle — it lacks the spine-of-four every cube net needs, so faces collide instead of closing. The other three are classic valid nets (cross, 3-3 staircase, 1-4-1).
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the solid 2×3 rectangle. Cube nets need four squares in a wraparound band; the rectangle's 2+2+2 stacking leaves two faces missing and two doubled. Cross, staircase, and mixed-row all contain valid folding spines.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Nets need a wraparound spine of four.
Count the band before trusting the shape.
Rectangles stack; cubes wrap — different topologies.
Invalid nets collide faces instead of closing.
Share this: cut one net and fold it tonight.

puzzles.title: The Southern Pip
puzzles.question: A standard die (opposite faces sum to 7) shows 5 on top and 3 facing north. Which number faces south?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 4 — north-south are opposites, so south is 7 minus 3. Top-bottom (5-2) never enters the calculation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 4. Opposite pairs sum to 7: north 3 forces south 4, whatever sits on top. Top-bottom information is pure distractor here.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Opposite pairs sum to seven, always.
North-south ignores top-bottom entirely.
Distractor faces test focus, not knowledge.
Pair before placing on every die question.
Share this: orient one die three ways fast.

puzzles.title: The Rolling Census
puzzles.question: A die shows 1 on top, 2 north, 3 east. It rolls east, then north, then east (tipping over each edge in turn). What number ends on top?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 6 — track faces through three tips: east puts 4 up... precisely east (top 4), north (top 5), east (top 6). Rolling permutations compose exactly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 6. Trace it: roll east (west face 4 rises to top), roll north (south face 5 rises), roll east (west face 6 rises). Each tip swaps four faces; composition does the rest.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Tips permute four faces and fix two.
Track tops through each roll stepwise.
Composition replaces visualization reliably.
East-then-north-then-east has one answer.
Share this: roll one die through three tips.

puzzles.title: The Punched Layers
puzzles.question: A sheet is folded in half, then in half again (four layers), and a hole is punched through all layers near the folded corner. Unfolded, how many holes show?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 4 — one punch through four layers makes four holes, mirrored across both fold lines. Layers multiply punctures exactly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 4. Each fold doubles the layers (2, then 4), and one punch marks every layer once. Unfolding mirrors the single hole across both creases into four.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Folds multiply layers; punches multiply holes.
Doubling twice quarters the paper into four.
Mirror across every crease to count.
Layers-times-punches is the whole formula.
Share this: punch one twice-folded sheet.

puzzles.title: The Right-Angle Count
puzzles.question: Between 12:00 and 12:00 (twelve hours), how many times do a clock's hands form an exact right angle?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 22 — right angles occur every ~65.45 minutes, twice per hour except the 2–4 stretch merges... precisely 22 in twelve hours (the 11th hour contributes none separately).
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 22. Twice hourly suggests 24, but the 2–3 and 3–4 right angles... the relative hand laps 11 times per 12 hours, yielding 22 perpendiculars. Overlapping cycles steal two from naive counting.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Naive doubling overcounts cyclic events.
Relative laps (11 per 12h) set the true count.
Perpendiculars come in pairs per lap.
Count cycles, not hours, for hand puzzles.
Share this: catch the missing right angles tonight.

puzzles.title: The Surface Shortcut
puzzles.question: An ant walks on the surface of a unit cube from one corner to the farthest opposite corner. What is the shortest surface distance?
puzzles.correctExplanation: √5 — unfold two adjacent faces into a 1×2 rectangle; the straight diagonal spans √(1+4). Surfaces flatten before measuring.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is √5 units. Through-space (√3) is forbidden; unfold two faces flat and the corner-to-corner straight line crosses a 1-by-2 rectangle. Flatten, then measure — never before.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Unfold surfaces before measuring shortcuts.
Rectangles replace cubes for path problems.
Straight lines on unfoldings are shortest paths.
Through-space answers betray surface rules.
Share this: unfold one box and draw the diagonal.

puzzles.title: The Dawn Polygon
puzzles.question: At sunrise, with light aimed along a cube's body diagonal, what shape is the cube's shadow on flat ground?
puzzles.correctExplanation: A regular hexagon — all six faces project equally around the diagonal axis. Symmetry of viewpoint dictates symmetry of shadow.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a hexagon. Face-on light gives squares, but diagonal light balances all six faces into six equal projected edges. Viewpoint symmetry transfers to shadow shape.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Viewpoint symmetry dictates shadow symmetry.
Diagonal views balance all six faces equally.
Six edges project where four stood.
Rotate the light, reshape the shadow.
Share this: shine one diagonal shadow tonight.

puzzles.title: The Orbiting Coin
puzzles.question: A coin rolls without slipping once around an identical stationary coin. How many full rotations does the rolling coin complete?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 2 — the center travels a circle of twice the radius (4πr path over 2πr circumference). Revolution adds to rotation: one for rolling, one for orbiting.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 2 rotations. Equal circumferences suggest one, but the center's orbit contributes a second full turn. Rolling-plus-revolving sums where pure rolling stands alone.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Orbits contribute rotations beyond rolling.
Center-path length divided by circumference counts.
Equal coins double, never single.
Revolution plus rotation always sums.
Share this: roll one coin around another.

puzzles.title: The Inner Orbit
puzzles.question: A coin rolls without slipping inside a ring of twice its diameter. How many rotations before returning to start?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 1 — inside, the orbit subtracts: center path πd over circumference πd... precisely (R−r)/r = 1. Interior rolling halves the exterior count.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 1 rotation. Inside the ring, revolution opposes rolling instead of adding: the hypocycloid of ratio 2:1 is a straight diameter, and the coin spins once. Outside doubles, inside singles.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Interior orbits subtract where exterior add.
Hypocycloids encode the subtraction exactly.
Ratio 2:1 draws diameters, not loops.
Inside-versus-outside flips the count.
Share this: roll one coin inside a ring.

puzzles.title: The Lifted Rope
puzzles.question: A rope hugging Earth's equator is lengthened by exactly 1 meter, then lifted uniformly all around. How high does it hover?
puzzles.correctExplanation: About 16 centimeters — gap equals extra length over 2π regardless of planet size (1/2π m). Earth's radius cancels completely out.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is about 16 centimeters. Circumference grows 2π per unit radius, so 1 meter buys 1/2π ≈ 0.16 m — on any sphere from marble to Jupiter. Bigness cancels; only the extra meter matters.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Radius cancels out of gap problems entirely.
Extra-over-2π is the universal hover formula.
Planet size never enters the answer.
Linearization defeats astronomical intuition.
Share this: lift one rope around one ball.

puzzles.title: The Moon Fold
puzzles.question: Standard paper (0.1 mm thick) folded repeatedly doubles each time. How many folds reach past the Moon (~384,400 km)?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 42 — 0.1mm × 2⁴² ≈ 440,000 km clears the Moon; 41 folds fall short at ~220,000 km. Exponentials humble linear intuition.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 42. Doubling 42 times multiplies thickness by four trillion; 41 folds reach only halfway to the Moon. Each fold is a doubling, and doublings compound violently.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Doublings compound beyond all intuition.
Forty-two doublings bridge Earth to Moon.
Linear guesses fail exponential questions.
Count doublings, never thickness, first.
Share this: fold one paper seven times max.

puzzles.title: The Caged Sphere
puzzles.question: What is the edge length of the largest cube that fits inside a unit sphere (diameter 2)?
choices: The square root of two units
puzzles.correctExplanation: Two over root three — the cube's space diagonal must equal the diameter: edge times root three equals 2. Corners touch sphere exactly at maximum fit.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is two over root three units. The limiting constraint is the body diagonal spanning the full diameter; edges follow by division. Inscribed means corners-kissing, and kissing sets the equation.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Diagonals, not edges, meet container walls.
Body-diagonal-equals-diameter constrains cubes.
Corners-kissing sets every fit equation.
Divide diagonals to recover edges.
Share this: cage one cube in one sphere.

puzzles.title: The Painted Edges
puzzles.question: A cube is painted red, then sliced into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 12 — the edge-centers excluding corners: 12 edges × 1 middle cube each. Two-face cubes live strictly mid-edge.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 12. Corners take three faces (8), face-centers take one (6), leaving edge-middles with exactly two: one per edge, twelve edges. Position classifies paint counts completely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Position classifies paint counts completely.
Corners three, edges two, faces one, core zero.
Count by location class, never by guessing.
Twelve edges means twelve two-facers.

puzzles.title: The Single Twist
puzzles.question: A paper Möbius band is cut along its center line all the way around. What results?
puzzles.correctExplanation: One loop twice as long (with two full twists) — the center line never meets an edge to separate. Half-twist topology refuses division.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is one longer loop. The cut rides the band's single surface without ever crossing an edge, so nothing separates — the band survives doubled in length, doubly twisted. One-sidedness preserves unity.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Center cuts ride surfaces without separating.
One-sided bands refuse to become two.
Length doubles where division was expected.
Topology overrides scissor intuition.

puzzles.title: The Utility Tangle
puzzles.question: Three houses must each connect to water, gas, and electricity with lines that never cross. On flat ground, is this possible?
puzzles.correctExplanation: No — K3,3 is provably nonplanar (Kuratowski): no crossing-free drawing exists on a plane. Curves don't help; only a handle (torus) would.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no, the graph is nonplanar. K3,3 defeats every layout trick — straight, curved, clever — on flat ground. Impossibility here is theorem, not lack of trying.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Impossibility can be theorem, not effort shortage.
K3,3 defeats all planar layouts provably.
Curves never rescue nonplanar graphs.
Handles (torus) change the game entirely.
Share this: tangle three houses on paper.

puzzles.title: The Tower Move
puzzles.question: The Tower of Hanoi with 6 disks must move as a stack between pegs, never placing larger on smaller. What is the minimum move count?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 63 — 2⁶−1 by the recursive optimum: move 5 (31), shift the largest (1), rebuild 5 (31). Doubling-plus-one governs every disk added.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 63. The recurrence M(n) = 2M(n−1)+1 with M(1)=1 yields 63 for six disks. Off-by-one answers (64, 32) forget the largest disk's single move or miscount the base.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Recurrence M(n)=2M(n−1)+1 governs towers.
Move n−1, shift largest, rebuild n−1.
Doubling-plus-one punishes every added disk.
Minimums prove by recursion, not experiment.
Share this: move three disks in seven tonight.

puzzles.title: The Cornerless Board
puzzles.question: Opposite corners are removed from a chessboard, leaving 62 squares. Can dominoes (each covering two adjacent squares) tile it exactly?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Impossible — removed corners share a color, leaving 32 of one and 30 of the other; each domino needs one of each. Color counts veto the tiling absolutely.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is impossible by color imbalance. Opposite corners match colors, so 62 squares split 32-30 while dominoes demand equality. Invariants beat attempts: no arrangement overcomes arithmetic.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Invariants veto constructions absolutely.
Color counts check tilings before attempts.
Dominoes demand equality square by square.
Removed corners unbalance the whole board.

puzzles.title: The Block Tower
puzzles.question: Cubes stack: a full 3×3 bottom layer, a centered 2×2 middle layer, and one cube centered on top. How many cubes total?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 14 — 9 + 4 + 1, every cube visible or supporting. Layer sums replace 3D visualization.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 14. Count by layers: 9 below, 4 mid, 1 crown. Centered stacking hides nothing here — all support is visible in the layer below.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Layer sums replace 3D visualization.
Count strata, never guess wholes.
Centered stacks hide nothing structural.
Nine-four-one is the classic pyramid.
Share this: stack one pyramid and count aloud.

puzzles.title: The Spun Word
puzzles.question: The word HOW is rotated 180° in the plane (each letter turns, and their order reverses). What do you read?
puzzles.correctExplanation: MOH — W becomes M, O stays O, H stays H, and reversed order gives M-O-H. Rotation transforms letters and positions together.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is MOH. Rotate each glyph (W→M, O→O, H→H) and reverse their order: W-O-H becomes M-O-H. Letter rotation plus position reversal compose the reading.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Rotations transform glyphs and orders together.
W→M while H,O survive the half-turn.
Reverse positions after turning letters.
Compose both moves before reading.

puzzles.title: The Inside Glove
puzzles.question: A right-hand glove is turned completely inside out. Which hand does it now fit?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The left hand — inside-out reverses chirality like a mirror. Thumb switches sides with the flip.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the left hand. Eversion mirrors handedness: the thumb that pointed left now points right. Inside-out is a reflection, and reflections swap chirality.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Eversion mirrors handedness exactly.
Inside-out acts as a reflection operator.
Thumbs switch sides with the flip.
Chirality swaps under mirror operations.
Share this: flip one glove tonight.

puzzles.title: The Polyhedron Census
puzzles.question: A convex polyhedron has 12 vertices and 20 faces. By Euler's formula (V − E + F = 2), how many edges?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 30 — 12 − E + 20 = 2 gives E = 30. Euler counts what eyes cannot.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 30. Plug into V − E + F = 2: 12 − E + 20 = 2, so E = 30. The dodecahedron-icosahedron family lives at these numbers.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Euler's formula counts the uncountable.
Plug vertices and faces; edges emerge.
V−E+F=2 governs all convex solids.
Arithmetic replaces visualization here.
