puzzles.title: The Unblocked Virtue
puzzles.question: 'Does what happened keep you from acting with justice, generosity, and truth? Then nothing blocks the good.' What must events never obstruct?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Virtuous action — externals touch circumstances, never character's output. Justice needs no permission from events.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is virtuous action. Happening cannot cancel character: generosity needs no favorable weather. Outputs stay sovereign whatever inputs suffer.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Character outputs need no weather permission.
Events touch settings, never virtues.
Justice operates in all climates.
Sovereignty lives in responses, not scenes.
Share this: act justly in bad weather.

puzzles.title: The Judgment Layer
puzzles.question: 'The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.' In this formula, what is a human life?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Opinion — life equals the mind's take, not the world's give. Change the take, change the life: idealism with work boots.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is opinion. Flux outside, verdict inside: living happens at the judgment layer. Takes can be retaken — that is the entire freedom.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Living happens at the judgment layer.
Takes retaken remake lives entirely.
Flux outside, verdict inside, always.
Idealism wears work boots here.
Share this: retake one verdict today.

puzzles.title: The Pain's Author
puzzles.question: 'If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is due to your estimate of it.' According to Marcus, what authors the distress?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Your estimate — externals propose, judgments dispose. Pain's authorship sits inside, whatever the occasion.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is your estimate. Events deliver raw material; valuations manufacture distress. Authorship implies editorship: re-estimate to relieve.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Valuations manufacture all distress suffered.
Raw material differs from finished pain.
Authorship implies editorship always.
Re-estimate to relieve genuinely.
Share this: re-estimate one distress today.

puzzles.title: The Worthy Bar
puzzles.question: Seneca warned that fearing death guarantees a specific failure: never doing anything worthy of a living person. What does death-fear prevent?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Worthy action — the fearful survive without living: breathing biographies, empty resumes. Boldness needs mortality faced.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is worthy action. Death-fear purchases safety at life's price: unrisked years sum to unlived ones. Worthiness demands the wager fear refuses.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Unrisked years sum to unlived ones.
Safety purchased costs life itself.
Worthiness demands wagers fear refuses.
Breathe biographies, or write them.
Share this: wager once worthily today.

puzzles.title: The Ample Years
puzzles.question: Seneca insisted life is not short but squandered — ample if well spent. Properly used, what is life's true length?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Life — length suffices; spending fails. Complaints about brevity confess prodigality.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is life. 'Short life' indicts the liver, never the lifespan: ample years poured down trivial drains. Audit spending before mourning supply.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Brevity complaints confess prodigality.
Supply suffices; spending fails reliably.
Audit outflows before mourning inflows.
Ample years await competent livers.
Share this: spend one hour un-squandered.

puzzles.title: The Lucky Meeting
puzzles.question: Seneca defined luck as the crossroads of two forces. When opportunity arrives, what must already be waiting?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Preparation — opportunity knocks for ready ears only. Luck favors the rehearsed, never the idle.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is preparation. Crossroads need both roads: chance arrives unbidden, readiness is built. Unprepared meetings are accidents, not luck.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Crossroads need both roads traveled.
Readiness converts accidents into luck.
Chance arrives; preparation receives.
Build before opportunity knocks.
Share this: prepare one unpromised meeting.

puzzles.title: The Inner Master
puzzles.question: 'No man is free who is not master of himself.' Epictetus makes freedom conditional on ruling what territory?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Oneself — self-mastery precedes all liberties: the unruled within obey every without. Kingdoms start at home or nowhere.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is oneself. External freedoms decorate internal servitude meaninglessly: appetites unruled make citizens of impulse. Rule within or be ruled without.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Internal servitude voids external freedoms.
Appetites unruled make impulse citizens.
Kingdoms start at home or nowhere.
Rule within first, always.
Share this: master one impulse today.

puzzles.title: The Revealing Storm
puzzles.question: Epictetus taught that circumstances don't make a person but expose them. What do hard times do to character?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Reveal character — storms display seams, never sew them. Pressure publishes what comfort drafts.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reveal character. Making implies creation; exposing implies prior existence. Blame the mirror, never the storm, for the face shown.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Storms publish what comfort drafts.
Pressure displays seams, never sews.
Mirrors blamed wrongly for faces shown.
Existence precedes exposure always.
Share this: read one storm's revelation.

puzzles.title: The Interrogation Rooms
puzzles.question: Two suspects, no communication: both silent gives 1 year each; both betray gives 3 each; lone betrayer walks while the loyal gets 5. If both reason selfishly and rationally, what happens?
choices: One betrays while the other stays silent
puzzles.correctExplanation: Both betray — defecting dominates: whatever the other does, betraying pays better individually. Mutual betrayal is the Nash equilibrium both regret.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is both betray, serving 3 years each. Check each cell: if your partner stays silent, betraying walks you (0 beats 1); if they betray, betraying cuts 5 to 3. Dominance decides regardless of sympathy.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Dominant strategies decide regardless of sympathy.
Equilibria can be regretted by everyone inside them.
Individual rationality aggregates into collective folly.
Map every cell before trusting solidarity.
Share this: interrogate two friends hypothetically tonight.

puzzles.title: The Copycat Champion
puzzles.question: Axelrod's computer tournaments pitted dozens of strategies in repeated dilemmas. Which disarmingly simple rule won twice?
choices: Tit-for-tat: cooperate first, then copy the opponent
puzzles.correctAnswer: Tit-for-tat: cooperate first, then copy the opponent
puzzles.correctExplanation: Tit-for-tat — nice, retaliatory, forgiving, clear. It never beats opponents head-to-head yet outscores them across tournaments by eliciting cooperation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is tit-for-tat: cooperate first, then copy the opponent. Defection wins battles; reciprocity wins tournaments. Clarity plus forgiveness outscored every clever exploitation scheme entered.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Nice, clear, retaliatory, forgiving: the winning quartet.
Tournaments reward eliciting, not extracting.
Simplicity beats cleverness across populations.
Copycats inherit cooperative worlds.

puzzles.title: The Long Shadow
puzzles.question: One-shot dilemmas end in betrayal, but repeated ones sustain cooperation. What does repetition add that changes everything?
choices: The rules rewrite themselves over time
puzzles.correctExplanation: Future retaliation — the shadow of coming rounds prices today's betrayal. Cooperation becomes self-interest once tomorrows matter.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is future retaliation disciplines present defection. Friendship, rule changes, and growing stakes are optional; consequences are structural. Lengthen shadows and cooperation follows.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Shadows of future rounds price present moves.
Consequences, not character, sustain cooperation.
Lengthen interactions to lengthen honesty.
Tomorrows mattering changes todays completely.
Share this: lengthen one relationship's shadow.

puzzles.title: The Shared Pasture
puzzles.question: Herder logic: adding one more cow gains its owner the full animal while the overgrazing cost spreads across all herders. What makes this rational individually and ruinous collectively?
choices: Each herder gains fully while sharing the damage
puzzles.correctAnswer: Each herder gains fully while sharing the damage
puzzles.correctExplanation: Full gains, shared damage — privatized benefits with socialized costs drive every herder to overstock. The pasture dies of individually sensible decisions.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is each herder gains fully while sharing the damage. Bans, fights, and weather miss the mechanism: asymmetric accounting. When I keep the cow and we share the bald field, baldness is arithmetic.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Privatized gains plus socialized costs ruin commons.
Asymmetric accounting drives overuse everywhere.
Sensible individuals compose ruined collectives.
Fix accounting before blaming herders.

puzzles.title: The Lobster Norms
puzzles.question: Maine lobstermen sustain catches for generations while open-access fisheries collapse. Researchers credit community enforcement, not just biology. What sustains the Maine catch?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Local monitoring plus graduated sanctions — Ostrom's design: watched waters plus penalties that escalate. Norms with teeth outlast fences without watchers.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is local monitoring plus graduated sanctions. Biology, feds, and temperature miss it: communities that watch and punish proportionally sustain what open access liquidates. Institutions, not oceans, decide.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Watched waters sustain what open access liquidates.
Penalties escalating beat punishments binary.
Institutions decide where biology merely enables.
Norms need teeth to hold teeth (lobster).

puzzles.title: The Free Listener
puzzles.question: Public radio is funded by voluntary pledges, yet non-payers hear every broadcast. What economic problem does the station face?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Free-riding — broadcasts can't exclude non-payers, so self-interest says listen free. Voluntary funding fights equilibrium constantly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is free-riding on non-excludable goods. Storms, regulators, and podcasts orbit the core: excludability missing means payment optional means underfunding chronic. Pledge drives beg against equilibria.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Non-excludable goods invite unpaid use.
Optional payment means chronic underfunding.
Pledge drives beg against equilibria.
Design funding that doesn't need angels.

puzzles.title: The Rejected Dollar
puzzles.question: A proposer splits $10; the responder can veto, leaving both with nothing. Pure rationality accepts even $1 — yet most humans reject low offers. What does rejection reveal?
choices: Fairness preferences overruling pure payoff maximization
puzzles.correctAnswer: Fairness preferences overruling pure payoff maximization
puzzles.correctExplanation: Fairness overrules maximization — responders pay to punish insulting splits. Utility includes dignity, not just dollars.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is fairness preferences overruling pure payoff maximization. Innumeracy, confusion, and spite miss it: costly punishment of unfairness is principled, predictable, and cross-cultural. Dollars aren't the only currency.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Dignity prices into every split offered.
Costly punishment polices fairness norms.
Utility includes insult, not just income.
Vetoes speak where acceptance would profit.

puzzles.title: The Quiet Gift
puzzles.question: A dictator splits $10 with a passive recipient who must accept anything. Pure rationality gives $0 — yet average gifts hover near $3. What does giving show?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Prosocial preferences without enforcement — dictators share with ghosts who cannot retaliate. Generosity precedes incentives.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is prosocial preferences operating without enforcement. No retaliation threatens, no error explains, no staff pays: giving flows from internalized norms. Humans arrive pre-loaded with fairness.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Generosity precedes incentives developmentally.
Ghosts receive real money from real dictators.
Internalized norms pay without police.
Pre-loaded fairness beats pure selfishness.

puzzles.title: The Tripled Trust
puzzles.question: An investor sends money that triples en route; the trustee may return any share. Strangers routinely send generously and receive fairly back. What sustains this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Reciprocity plus reputational shadow — trust extended expects return, and social worlds punish betrayal. Tripling tempts; norms restrain.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reciprocity norms plus reputational shadow. No contracts bind, no twins play, no fakes circulate: strangers trust because social species keep ledgers. Returns reward the brave senders.

Social species keep invisible ledgers always.
Tripling tempts; norms restrain reliably.
Trust extended expects return by default.
Shadows of reputation discipline strangers.

puzzles.title: The Shaky Partner
puzzles.question: Two hunters can jointly take a stag (feast) or solo a hare (snack). If your partner might wander, what tempts you toward the smaller prize?
choices: The safe hare when the partner seems shaky
puzzles.correctAnswer: The safe hare when the partner seems shaky
puzzles.correctExplanation: The safe hare — stag pays best only with trusted coordination; doubt discounts it. Risk-dominant safety beats payoff-dominant glory under uncertainty.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the safe hare when the partner seems shaky. Laziness, taste, and superstition miss it: trust levels select equilibria. Rousseau's hunters teach that confidence coordinates, doubt defects.

Trust levels select equilibria directly.
Confidence coordinates; doubt defects.
Safety tempts exactly when partners wobble.
Payoff-dominance needs trust to activate.

puzzles.title: The Headlight Game
puzzles.question: Two drivers race straight at each other; first to swerve loses face, neither swerving wrecks both. Nuclear crises ran this exact script. What game is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Chicken — winning means convincing the other you'll never swerve. Brinkmanship weaponizes apparent irrationality: the stronger the commitment, the stronger the leverage.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is chicken: brinkmanship with catastrophic ties. Cooperation, dances, and grids mislabel it: losers swerve, winners risk everything, ties kill. Credible craziness is the equilibrium strategy.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Credible craziness leverages rational opponents.
Swerve-losses price against crash-losses.
Commitment devices win staring contests.
Apparent irrationality can be strategy.

puzzles.title: The Station Meeting
puzzles.question: Separated partners must reunite somewhere in New York with zero communication. Most pairs independently choose the same famous spot at noon. What coordinated them?
choices: A focal point salient to both minds
puzzles.correctAnswer: A focal point salient to both minds
puzzles.correctExplanation: A focal point — Grand Central at noon stands out symmetrically: each expects the other to expect it. Salience substitutes for communication.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a focal point salient to both minds. No telepathy, agreements, or trackers: shared culture makes one option conspicuous to both. Schelling points coordinate the incommunicado.

Salience substitutes for communication elegantly.
Shared culture spotlights meeting places.
Expectations of expectations converge fast.
Conspicuous options coordinate strangers.

puzzles.title: The Side Choice
puzzles.question: A country must standardize driving on the left or the right; either works if everyone complies. What kind of solution does this need?
choices: Scientific proof of the better side
puzzles.correctExplanation: A shared convention — coordination needs agreement, not optimality. Left and right tie on merits; unanimity breaks all ties.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a shared convention, either side. Science, history, and instinct miss it: content is arbitrary, commonality essential. Conventions solve by synchronizing, never by optimizing.

Agreement beats optimality in coordination.
Arbitrary content, essential commonality.
Conventions synchronize; they never optimize.
Unanimity breaks all substantive ties.

puzzles.title: The Pump War
puzzles.question: Two gas stations undercut each other until margins hit zero, though both earned more at high prices. What trapped these competitors?
choices: Mutual defection as the only equilibrium

puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is mutual defection as the only equilibrium. Oil, loyalty, and regulators orbit the core: unilateral high prices get undercut instantly. Preferred matrices collapse without enforcement.

Preferred outcomes collapse without enforcement.
Undercutting ratchets prices to cost.
Unilateral virtue gets punished promptly.
Equilibria ignore everyone's preferences.

puzzles.title: The Secret Barrel
puzzles.question: Cartel members pledge output quotas to hold prices high, yet each can profit by secretly pumping extra at the cartel price. What tempts every member?
choices: Full price for one's own extra barrels
puzzles.correctAnswer: Full price for one's own extra barrels
puzzles.correctExplanation: Full price for secret extras — the cheater sells cartel-priced oil in cartel-breaking volume. Quotas bind everyone except, marginally, you.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is full price for one's own extra barrels. Loyalty, boycotts, and meetings miss the math: extra volume at held-high prices is irresistible individually, fatal collectively. Cartels die of private arithmetic.

Private arithmetic kills public agreements.
Held prices plus secret volume tempts all.
Quotas bind everyone except marginally you.
Cartels need monitors, not just handshakes.

puzzles.title: The Smokestack Pact
puzzles.question: Two hundred nations all gain if all cut emissions, while each gains most by polluting as others cut. Climate talks stall in exactly this structure. What is it?
choices: A coordination game with easy fixes
puzzles.correctExplanation: An N-player prisoner's dilemma — universal cutting beats universal polluting, but defecting dominates each seat. Scale multiplies the original two-person trap.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is an N-player prisoner's dilemma. Misunderstandings and easy fixes deny the structure: every nation faces the interrogation room with 199 partners. Treaties must rewrite payoffs, not just plead.

Scale multiplies classic traps undiminished.
Two-person logic governs 200-seat rooms.
Pleadings fail where payoffs rule.
Treaties must rewrite, never merely request.

puzzles.title: The Miracle Jar
puzzles.question: Each antibiotic course cures its patient while slightly eroding drug effectiveness for everyone future. What kind of good is antibiotic effectiveness?
choices: A commons depleted by individually rational use
A private good owned by pharmacists
puzzles.correctAnswer: A commons depleted by individually rational use
puzzles.correctExplanation: A depleting commons — each prescription is correct for its patient and corrosive for the future. Effectiveness is shared pasture grazed by prescriptions.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a commons depleted by individually rational use. Ownership, infinity, and luxury misclassify: cures consume future cures. Stewardship means sometimes withholding working drugs.

Cures consume future cures measurably.
Correct-for-patient can corrode-for-all.
Shared pastures include invisible medicines.
Stewardship sometimes withholds working drugs.

puzzles.title: The Pledge Threshold
puzzles.question: A fundraiser charges cards only if 500 donors join — nobody risks paying alone for a failed project. What mechanism removes the sucker's risk?
puzzles.correctExplanation: A dominant assurance contract — pledging is safe (no charge if short) and decisive (your pledge may complete the threshold). Tabarrok's fix makes cooperation the easy choice.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a dominant assurance contract. Guilt, fame, and prizes orbit the core mechanism: conditional charging deletes downside while preserving upside. Assure first, collect after.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Conditional charging deletes downside risk.
Thresholds convert pledges into pivotal acts.
Assure first; collect only on success.
Mechanisms beat moralizing for funding.

puzzles.title: The Eternal Grudge
puzzles.question: One strategy cooperates until any defection, then defects forever after. In repeated games, what does this grim posture threaten?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Permanent retaliation — one strike ends cooperation eternally. Grim threats sustain peace precisely by being unthinkable to trigger.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is permanent retaliation for any deviation. Forgiveness variants soften other strategies; grim's whole power is irreversibility. Eternity deters what proportion forgets.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Irreversibility deters what proportion forgets.
Eternal threats sustain fragile peaces.
One strike ends worlds under grim rules.
Unthinkable consequences govern thinkable acts.

puzzles.title: The Forgiving Copy
puzzles.question: In noisy tournaments where moves get misread, plain copycatting spirals into endless feuds from single errors. What modification wins instead?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Occasional forgiveness — generous tit-for-tat absorbs errors instead of echoing them. Noise demands shock absorbers, not louder echoes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is occasional forgiveness breaking retaliation spirals. Never-retaliate gets exploited, harsher echoes amplify static, quitting forfeits everything. Generosity is error-correction for strategies.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Noise demands shock absorbers in strategies.
Echoes amplify static; forgiveness filters it.
Errors need absorption, never mirroring.
Generosity error-corrects retaliation.

puzzles.title: The Staying Rule
puzzles.question: Win-stay-lose-shift repeats whatever just paid and abandons whatever just failed — no memory beyond last round. Under noisy conditions this outperforms copycatting. What is the rule?
choices: Stay on wins, shift on losses
puzzles.correctAnswer: Stay on wins, shift on losses
puzzles.correctExplanation: Stay on wins, shift on losses — Pavlov corrects its own mistakes where tit-for-tat echoes noise. One-round memory beats grudges in static.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is stay on wins, shift on losses. Initial cooperation, rigidity, and double-copying miss it: outcome-contingent switching self-repairs. Pavlov salivates at rewards and abandons punishments.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Outcome-contingent switching self-repairs fast.
One-round memory beats eternal grudges.
Rewards repeated; punishments abandoned.
Simplicity with feedback beats memory with spite.

puzzles.title: The Good Name
puzzles.question: Donors give generously to strangers known to have given to others — cooperation sustained without any repeated meetings. What mechanism carries it?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Indirect reciprocity — image scores circulate: help the helpful, and helpers help you. Reputation extends reciprocity beyond pairs.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is indirect reciprocity through reputations. Kinship, welfare, and force miss it: strangers cooperate via gossip ledgers. 'I help you because you helped them' scales kindness to societies.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Gossip ledgers scale kindness to societies.
Image scores circulate like currency.
Help-the-helpful rules need no repeats.
Reputation extends reciprocity past pairs.

puzzles.title: The Fixed Split
puzzles.question: Press and Dyson discovered strategies letting one player unilaterally enforce a fixed, unfair payoff ratio against any adapting opponent. What do these extortionate strategies enforce?
puzzles.correctExplanation: A lopsided ratio, unilaterally — zero-determinant strategies pin the opponent's payoff to your own terms. Mathematics permits what morals condemn.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a lopsided payoff ratio unilaterally. Equality, welfare, and fairness miss it: extortionate ZD play sets the exchange rate by fiat. Opponents adapt; the ratio stands.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Mathematics permits what morals condemn.
Ratios set by fiat survive adaptation.
Unilateral pinning beats mutual bargaining.
Exchange rates can be dictated, not just dealt.

puzzles.title: The Tipping Pool
puzzles.question: In collective-risk experiments, groups facing a catastrophic tipping point contribute far more when the danger is high, clear, and shared. What drives the contributions?
choices: Perceived catastrophic risk with clear thresholds
puzzles.correctAnswer: Perceived catastrophic risk with clear thresholds
puzzles.correctExplanation: Perceived catastrophic risk with clear thresholds — Milinski's pools fill when doom is vivid and the line visible. Clarity plus stakes manufacture cooperation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is perceived catastrophic risk with clear thresholds. Selflessness, mandates, and ignorance miss it: transparent danger focuses minds that foggy danger frees. Draw bright lines around cliffs.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Bright lines around cliffs focus minds.
Vivid doom funds prevention generously.
Foggy dangers free-ride; clear ones compel.
Thresholds convert crowds into crews.

puzzles.title: The Costly Ballot
puzzles.question: A single vote essentially never decides large elections, yet millions pay real costs to cast one. What best explains mass turnout?
choices: Expressive and norm-driven motives beyond pivotality
puzzles.correctAnswer: Expressive and norm-driven motives beyond pivotality
puzzles.correctExplanation: Expressive and norm-driven motives — voters speak values and honor duty; pivotality never enters it. Ballots are voices, not levers.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is expressive and norm-driven motives beyond pivotality. Innumeracy, bribery, and coercion miss most turnout: citizens vote to be the kind of people who vote. Identity outbids instrumentality at the polls.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Identity outbids instrumentality at polls.
Ballots voice values; they rarely lever outcomes.
Duty speaks where pivotality stays silent.
Vote to be voters, not to decide.

puzzles.title: The Blind Weigher
puzzles.question: Blindfolded I weigh every soul alike, yet my sword never sleeps. Courts carve me over doors I never enter. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Justice — blind weighing plus unsleeping sword plus courthouse carvings. Emblems assemble the abstraction.

Courts carve me above their doors.
My blindfold promises impartial weight.
Swords in my hand never sleep.

Emblems assemble abstractions piece by piece.
Blindfolds promise impartiality everywhere.
Civic carvings confirm institutional readings.
Attributes plus habitat name the concept.

puzzles.title: The Unheld Bird
puzzles.question: Cage me and I die; release me and I stay. Prisoners dream me while tyrants fear my name. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Freedom — dying in cages, staying when released, dreamed by prisoners. The bird that perishes when held.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is freedom. Cage-kills plus release-stays isolates what exists only unheld; prisoner-dreams and tyrant-fears confirm the political reading.
puzzles.hintText:
Cages kill me; open skies keep me.
Prisoners dream me nightly.
Tyrants fear my very name.

Die-when-held marks unownable goods.
Dreamers and fearers triangulate abstractions.
Release-stays inverts possession logic.

puzzles.title: The Naked Runner
puzzles.question: Clothed in proof I slow to a walk; naked I outrun every lie. Courts demand me but rarely host me. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Truth — outrunning lies, slowed by proof's clothing, demanded yet absent in courts. Nakedness is speed here.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is truth. Lie-outrunning plus proof-clothing plus court-demanding assembles the concept: reality unadorned travels fastest. Nakedness means unmediated, not undressed.

Proof clothes me but slows my pace.
Courts demand what they rarely host.

Proof clothes but also slows.
Demand-plus-absence marks institutions' ideals.
Nakedness means unmediated here.

puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the embryo from dietary toxins. Comfort, bonding, and revenues miss it: timing plus targets reveal defense. Morning sickness guards mornings that matter.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Timing plus targets reveal defenses.
Misery can carry protective assignments.
Bitter-and-meat aversions guard development.
Nausea bodyguards the vulnerable weeks.

puzzles.title: The Narrow Gate
puzzles.question: Human birth is uniquely perilous: big-brained infants must pass pelvises narrowed for upright walking. What evolutionary trade-off causes this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Brains versus bipedal pelvises — the obstetric dilemma: encephalization pushed up, locomotion pushed in. Birth pain is geometry, not failure.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is brains versus bipedal pelvises. Doctors, growth rates, and diets miss it: walking upright narrowed the gate that thinking widened. Peril is the compromise made flesh.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Geometry, not failure, explains birth peril.
Encephalization pushed; locomotion constrained.
Compromises made flesh hurt by design.
Narrow gates plus big heads equal drama.

puzzles.title: The Grandmother Dividend
puzzles.question: Human females live decades past fertility — nearly unique among primates. The grandmother hypothesis says post-reproductive years pay through what?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Grandchildren surviving better — experienced alloparents raise grandoffspring survival enough to select for longevity itself. Menopause funds grandmothers.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is grandchildren surviving better. Aging, wealth, and appetite miss it: post-fertile help boosts descendants' fitness directly. Longevity evolved through grandchildren's eyes.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Post-fertile help boosts descendant fitness.
Longevity evolved through grandchildren's survival.
Alloparents fund their own selection.
Menopause is strategy, never malfunction.
Share this: thank one grandmother dividend.

puzzles.title: The Early Peanut
puzzles.question: Avoiding peanuts increased childhood allergy rates; feeding peanuts early (LEAP trial) cut allergy ~80%. What builds the tolerance?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Early oral exposure — the gut taught tolerance while avoidance taught alarm. Timing, not dose, decides allergy curricula.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is early oral exposure building tolerance. Bans and delays backfired: immune systems learn friend from food by meeting it early. Windows open, then close — feed accordingly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Windows open briefly, then close firmly.
Guts teach tolerance by early meeting.
Avoidance curricula graduate alarmists.
Timing decides allergy outcomes most.
Share this: feed windows, not fears.

puzzles.title: The Loud Hours
puzzles.question: Ears evolved for transient natural sounds, not hours of high-decibel streams. Chronic loud listening destroys first and irreversibly what?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Inner-ear hair cells — mammalian cochleae don't regrow them. Transient design meets continuous assault; silence can't restore the dead.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is inner-ear hair cells. Skin, skull, and nose miss it: the transducers themselves die without replacement. Volume limits are design limits, not suggestions.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Transducers die without replacement parts.
Design limits are not suggestions.
Continuous assaults break transient machinery.
Silence restores nothing dead.
Share this: lower one volume today.

puzzles.title: The Snapping Gaze
puzzles.question: Phones farm the orienting response — attention snapping to novelty, motion, and alerts. Brains built for savanna surprises now serve whom?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The novelty-detection reflex — orienting to movement and pings once spotted predators; now it spots notifications. Savanna alarms ring for silicon.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the novelty-detection reflex. Knees, modes, and dives miss it: snap-to-novelty kept foragers alive and keeps users scrolling. Alerts are artificial predators of attention.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Snap-to-novelty kept foragers alive.
Alerts are artificial attention predators.
Savanna alarms ring for silicon now.
Reflexes serve whoever triggers them.
Share this: starve one artificial predator.

puzzles.title: The Blunt Index
puzzles.question: BMI brands muscular athletes obese and frail lightweights healthy. As a health gauge, what does the index completely ignore?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Body composition — mass over height-squared cannot see muscle versus fat. Blunt indices misclassify both tails.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is body composition entirely. Height, age, and timing miss it: the formula lacks any fat-versus-lean term. Populations average fine; individuals deserve better gauges.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Formulas lacking terms misclassify tails.
Muscle and fat weigh identically here.
Population tools fail individual cases.
Composition, not mass, decides health.
Share this: retire one blunt index.

puzzles.title: The Broken Clock
puzzles.question: Night-shift workers carry higher metabolic and cancer risks; WHO flags circadian disruption as probably carcinogenic. What does chronic desync damage?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Clock-coordinated physiology — hormones, repair, and cell cycles run on circadian timetables that shift work scrambles. Desync is systemic, not sleepiness.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is clock-coordinated physiology. Pay, calendars, and alarms miss it: bodies schedule repair and division by light-dark cycles. Scrambling timetables breaks more than mornings.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Bodies schedule repairs by light cycles.
Scrambling timetables breaks systemically.
Desync exceeds mere sleepiness vastly.
Timetables are physiological, not social.
Share this: guard one circadian edge.

puzzles.title: The Longer Day
puzzles.question: Eastward flights (losing hours) punish travelers more than equal westward ones. The brain's internal day runs slightly longer than 24 hours. Why does this asymmetry matter?
choices: The brain's day runs slightly long
puzzles.correctAnswer: The brain's day runs slightly long
puzzles.correctExplanation: The internal day runs ~24.2 hours — delaying (westward) rides the natural drift; advancing (eastward) fights it. Direction matters because clocks have grain.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the brain's day runs slightly long. Food, politics, and luggage miss it: phase delays cooperate with biology while advances oppose it. Fly with the drift when possible.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Internal days exceed 24 hours slightly.
Delays cooperate; advances oppose.
Direction matters because clocks have grain.
Fly with biological drift when possible.
Share this: delay, don't advance, once.

puzzles.title: The Atomized Tribe
puzzles.question: Tribal brains marooned in atomized cities report record loneliness with measurable cardiac and immune costs. What mismatch drives the epidemic?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Band-sized needs in mass society — belonging systems built for dense kin networks starve among millions of strangers. Crowds don't cure tribal hunger.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is band-sized needs meeting mass society. Excess friends, empathy, and reunions miss it: contact without belonging starves the system. Density differs from community entirely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Contact without belonging starves systems.
Density differs from community entirely.
Crowds never cure tribal hunger.
Belonging needs bands, not masses.
Share this: band one stranger today.

puzzles.title: The Exaggerated Lure
puzzles.question: Tinbergen's birds preferred giant painted eggs over their own; junk food, feeds, and pornography exploit the same glitch. What defines a supernormal stimulus?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Exaggeration beyond natural maxima — instincts calibrated to wild ranges misfire on amplified fakes. Bigger buttons press harder, truthfully or not.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is exaggeration beyond natural maxima. Naturalness, noise, and deprivation miss it: preferences evolved over real ranges get hijacked past their peaks. Calibration breaks past maxima.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Calibrations break past natural maxima.
Bigger buttons press harder, truly or falsely.
Hijacked instincts misfire on fakes.
Wild ranges bound honest preferences.
Share this: spot one exaggerated lure.

puzzles.title: The Maximum Voltage
puzzles.question: In Milgram's baseline setup, about two-thirds of ordinary participants delivered the maximum 450-volt shock when the experimenter instructed them to continue.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Roughly 65% went to 450V despite protests, sweating, and screams. Ordinary people, extraordinary compliance.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The baseline number — 26 of 40 to maximum — shocked psychology itself. Protests accompanied obedience; almost nobody enjoyed it, yet most continued.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Ordinary people comply extraordinarily under authority.
Protests accompany obedience more than prevent it.
Baselines anchor every variation after.
Two-thirds is the number that changed ethics.
Share this: quote 65% before judging anyone.

puzzles.title: The Closer Victim
puzzles.question: Moving the suffering learner into the same room as the teacher increased obedience, since closeness builds empathy that overrides orders.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Proximity collapsed obedience (to ~40%, touch-proximity ~30%): closeness empowers refusal, not compliance. Distance enables harm.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Same-room suffering cut obedience sharply; forced touch cut it further. Empathy needs proximity to activate — remote victims suffer most from compliance.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Proximity empowers refusal reliably.
Distance enables harm more than closeness.
Empathy needs nearness to activate.
Remote suffering obeys smoothest.
Share this: close one distance deliberately.

puzzles.title: The Phone Orders
puzzles.question: When the experimenter issued orders by telephone instead of standing nearby, obedience rates stayed essentially identical to baseline.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Absent authority collapsed compliance to ~20%: many participants improvised lower shocks or quit. Presence pressures; distance liberates.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Telephone orders bled authority badly — a fifth obeyed versus two-thirds present. Voices without bodies command weakly; proximity is pressure.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Presence pressures; absence liberates measurably.
Voices without bodies command weakly.
Authority attenuates across distance fast.
Nearness is pressure's delivery system.
Share this: hang up on one remote order.

puzzles.title: The Divided Coats
puzzles.question: When two experimenters visibly disagreed about continuing, obedience fell to nearly zero — every participant stopped and sided against cruelty.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Divided authority paralyzes compliance: with no single legitimate voice, participants halted. Unity commands; disagreement frees.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Two lab coats arguing collapsed the spell completely — zero full obedience. Legitimacy needs unanimity; visible dissent among authorities liberates subjects instantly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Divided authorities liberate subjects instantly.
Unanimity is legitimacy's load-bearing wall.
Visible dissent breaks spells completely.
Two coats arguing free every teacher.
Share this: voice one dissent that frees others.

puzzles.title: The Rebelling Peers
puzzles.question: Adding two confederate 'teachers' who refuse to continue had little effect — real participants kept obeying at baseline rates regardless.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Peer rebellion crashed obedience to ~10%: seeing refusal modeled made refusing possible. One dissenter frees dozens silently waiting.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Confederate refusers demolished compliance — modeling dissent matters more than feeling it. Permission structures, not private doubts, decide obedience.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Modeled dissent matters more than felt doubt.
One refuser frees dozens silently waiting.
Permission structures decide obedience rates.
Peers outweigh experimenters in courage markets.

puzzles.title: The Seedy Office
puzzles.question: Moving the experiment from prestigious Yale to a run-down Bridgeport office made essentially no difference to obedience rates.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Bridgeport obedience fell to ~48%: prestige legitimizes cruelty measurably. Lab coats need impressive buildings behind them.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Yale's marble bought seventeen extra points of compliance over a shabby storefront. Legitimacy cues — architecture included — calibrate obedience precisely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Marble buys compliance measurably.
Prestige legitimizes cruelty point by point.
Settings calibrate obedience precisely.
Storefronts free what campuses bind.

puzzles.title: The German Question
puzzles.question: Follow-up studies across cultures found obedience effects broadly similar outside America — the pattern was never a German or American specialty.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Replications from Munich to Amman to Australia return comparable rates: situations, not national characters, drive compliance. No culture holds a monopoly on obedience.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The 'authoritarian culture' excuse died in replication: Jordanians, Germans, Australians obeyed alike. Situations export perfectly; dispositions explain little.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Situations export; characters stay local.
Replication kills cultural excuses cleanly.
No nation monopolizes obedience or defiance.
Human is the relevant nationality here.
Share this: retire one national stereotype.

puzzles.title: The Modern Cap
puzzles.question: Jerry Burger's 2009 partial replication — stopping at 150 volts for ethics — found obedience patterns closely matching Milgram's era.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Capped at the 150V decision point, modern participants refused at nearly identical rates to 1960s ones. Decades changed ethics rules, not human responses.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Burger's ethical redesign preserved the crucial comparison: pre-150V behavior matched across half a century. Modernity flatters itself; the lab does not.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Decades change rules, rarely responses.
Capped replications preserve crucial comparisons.
Modernity flatters itself without evidence.
150 volts still divides eras identically.
Share this: doubt one 'we've evolved' claim.

puzzles.title: The Television Volt
puzzles.question: A French TV show replicated Milgram as a game show, with an audience cheering — and obedience ran even higher, near 80%.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. 'Game of Death' showed cameras plus crowds outrank lab coats: 64 of 80 shocked to maximum. Entertainment legitimizes what science merely requests.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Beauvois's televised version out-obeyed Yale: audiences and spotlights added authority no ethics board approved. Applause commands louder than clipboards.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Applause commands louder than clipboards.
Cameras add authority ethics never approved.
Entertainment legitimizes beyond science.
Crowds amplify orders measurably.

puzzles.title: The Agent Excuse
puzzles.question: Milgram argued participants entered an 'agentic state' — seeing themselves as instruments of authority, responsibility shifted upward.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The agentic shift explains the catchphrase 'just following orders': self as instrument, authority as author. Responsibility outsourced feels like responsibility absent.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Subjects repeatedly said the experimenter was responsible — agency transferred, conscience muted. Instruments don't deliberate; that was precisely the state induced.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Instruments don't deliberate by definition.
Responsibility outsourced feels absent entirely.
Agentic shifts mute private conscience.
Authorship assigned upward absolves downward.
Share this: reclaim one outsourced agency.

puzzles.title: The Shifted Blame
puzzles.question: When debriefed, obedient participants typically claimed full personal responsibility and rejected any suggestion the experimenter shared blame.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Participants overwhelmingly assigned responsibility to the experimenter ('he told me to'): blame flowed upward, never inward.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Debriefings record blame flowing upward: subjects insisted the experimenter owned the consequences. Responsibility shifted exactly as the agentic theory predicts — outward, upward, away.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Blame flows upward under authority reliably.
'I was told to' is the agentic motto.
Outward, upward, away: blame's escape route.
Ownership evaporates inside hierarchies.
Share this: own one ordered act fully.

puzzles.title: The Universal Obedience
puzzles.question: Milgram's headline finding was that essentially all participants obeyed to the maximum — disobedience was vanishingly rare.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Thirty-five percent refused outright — heroes exist in every condition. Headlines remember the obedient; data honors the refusers too.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Fourteen of forty defied the experimenter completely at baseline. Obedience dominated but never monopolized: minorities refuse in all conditions.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Minorities refuse in all conditions studied.
Headlines remember sheep; data keeps goats.
Thirty-five percent is a large resistance.
Honor refusers alongside the obedient.
Share this: join one baseline minority.

puzzles.title: The Scream Stopper
puzzles.question: The learner's agonized screams and demands to be freed ended the session for most participants, who stopped shocking immediately.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Screams accompanied continued shocking for the majority — protests without exit. Agony registered; compliance continued anyway.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The 300-volt wall of protest stopped almost nobody: two-thirds marched past screams to 450V. Hearing suffering differs entirely from heeding it.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hearing differs entirely from heeding.
Screams accompany compliance routinely.
Protest without exit changes nothing.
Agony registered still gets overridden.
Share this: heed one scream fully.

puzzles.title: The Gender Gap
puzzles.question: Milgram found women obeyed at dramatically lower rates than men, suggesting conscience tracks gender strongly.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. An all-female run matched male rates (~65%): conscience shows no gender gap under authority. Stereotypes of gentler refusal died in the data.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Women obeyed identically (though with more visible distress): situation swamps gender completely. Gentler-sex theories found no support in the voltage logs.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Situations swamp gender completely here.
Distress differs; compliance matches exactly.
Stereotypes die in voltage logs.
Conscience shows no gender gap found.
Share this: retire one gendered virtue claim.

puzzles.title: The Born Follower
puzzles.question: Authoritarian personality scores strongly predicted who obeyed — dispositions, not situations, drove Milgram's results.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Personality predicted weakly; condition variations predicted massively. Milgram's thesis is situational: contexts, not characters, explain compliance.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. F-scale scores barely moved the needle while room layouts swung obedience forty points. Dispositions decorate; situations decide — the field's founding lesson.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Contexts decide where characters decorate.
Room layouts swing forty points easily.
Personality barely moves obedience needles.
Situations explain; dispositions describe.
Share this: blame one room, not one soul.

puzzles.title: The Willing Sadist
puzzles.question: Milgram's volunteers were disproportionately sadistic — they enjoyed delivering pain, which explains the high obedience rates.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Participants sweated, trembled, protested, and begged to stop — enjoyment was vanishingly rare. Obedience tortured the obedient too.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Observers record anguish, not pleasure: nervous laughter, seizures of tension, desperate glances. Compliance without joy is precisely what makes the finding terrifying.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Anguish accompanied obedience routinely.
Enjoyment was vanishingly rare throughout.
Compliance tortures the compliant too.
Joyless obedience terrifies most of all.
Share this: pity one obedient sufferer.

puzzles.title: The Grateful Subject
puzzles.question: In follow-up surveys, the large majority of Milgram's participants said they were glad to have taken part, with almost none regretting it.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Roughly 84% reported gladness versus ~1% regret: subjects valued the self-knowledge purchased with distress. Ethics debates rage; participants mostly endorsed.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Follow-ups show overwhelming endorsement: painful afternoons bought lasting insight most prized. Debriefings plus time converted trauma into education, by subjects' own accounts.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Distress purchased insight most prized.
Endorsement followed debriefing plus time.
Subjects judge ethics by their own lights.
Painful afternoons educated willingly.
Share this: ask what distress taught you.

puzzles.title: The Consent Legacy
puzzles.question: Outrage over Milgram's deception helped drive modern informed-consent rules and ethics boards governing human research.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Deception without full consent became the cautionary tale behind IRBs and consent codes. One lab's methods rewrote every lab's permissions.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Baumrind's critiques plus public shock converted Milgram into regulation: review boards now gatekeep human studies worldwide. Controversy institutionalized into procedure.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Controversy institutionalizes into procedure.
Cautionary tales rewrite permissions globally.
Deception debates built modern gates.
One lab reformed ten thousand.
Share this: thank one ethics board.

puzzles.title: The Ordinary Finding
puzzles.question: Milgram's core conclusion was that horrific obedience requires disturbed or evil personalities — monsters, not neighbors.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. The conclusion inverts it: ordinary neighbors suffice — situations manufacture compliance from the unremarkable. Monstrousness is optional equipment.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. 'Just ordinary people' is the terrifying thesis: no pathology required, no sadism needed. Neighbors suffice wherever authority structures the scene.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Neighbors suffice where monsters were assumed.
Unremarkable people comply remarkably.
Pathology is optional equipment here.
Ordinary is the terrifying finding.
Share this: suspect one ordinary neighbor (lovingly).

puzzles.title: The Nearby Coat
puzzles.question: Obedience held steady whether the experimenter stood beside the teacher or issued orders from another room entirely.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Nearby authority compels; distant authority merely suggests (65% versus ~20%). Steadiness across distance is precisely what the data refutes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Same-room orders versus telephone orders differ massively (~65% vs ~20%): nearness is pressure. This statement claims steadiness across distance, which the data refutes.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Nearness is pressure, measurably.
Distance liberates measurably too.
Steadiness claims fail against gradients.
Coats nearby compel; phones suggest.

puzzles.title: The White Coat
puzzles.question: Symbols of legitimate expertise — lab coats, clipboards, prestigious addresses — measurably raise compliance with instructions.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Legitimacy cues calibrate obedience: coats, titles, and marble each buy compliance points. Authority dresses for the effect it wants.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Yale versus storefront, uniform versus casual: trappings move needles reliably. Costumes command because minds outsource vetting to symbols.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Costumes command reliably worldwide.
Symbols outsource vetting efficiently.
Marble, coats, titles: compliance wardrobe.
Dress cues calibrate obedience points.
Share this: undress one authority symbol.

puzzles.title: The Small Steps
puzzles.question: The 15-volt increments — tiny escalations from trivial to terrible — helped participants advance without ever deciding to do great harm.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Gradual escalation dissolves decision points: each step is only slightly worse than the last accepted one. No single shock feels like the moral cliff.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Foot-in-the-door electrified: 15 volts more is always agreeable until 450. Great harms arrive in small, each-time-reasonable increments.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Great harms arrive incrementally always.
Decision points dissolve under gradients.
Slightly-worse compounds into terrible.
Watch each step, not just cliffs.

puzzles.title: The Many Rooms
puzzles.question: Milgram ran only one single experimental setup, so his findings rest on a single unrepeated observation.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Milgram ran twenty-plus variations — proximity, prestige, peers, settings — mapping obedience's gradients systematically. Single setups never supported the thesis.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. The book reports a program, not an experiment: dozens of conditions isolate each variable. Replication lives inside the original work itself.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Programs persuade where experiments suggest.
Dozens of conditions map gradients fully.
Variation is replication's first home.
Single setups never carried this thesis.

puzzles.title: The Nightingale Orders
puzzles.question: In Hofling's hospital study, almost all nurses prepared to obey an unknown doctor's dangerous phone order — 21 of 22 began compliance.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. White coats by telephone commanded 95% initial compliance despite rule violations. Hospitals run on hierarchy deeper than protocol.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Unknown voice, broken rules, lethal dose — yet white-coat authority overrode training in nearly every nurse. Hierarchy outranks protocol wherever coats speak.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hierarchy outranks protocol routinely.
Unknown voices command through coats.
Training yields to titles under pressure.
White coats override rulebooks daily.

puzzles.title: The Assigned Cruelty
puzzles.question: In Zimbardo's Stanford prison study, randomly assigned guards developed abusive behaviors within days, shaped by roles and setting.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Random assignment plus uniforms plus basement produced cruelty in under a week — stopped early for ethics. Roles recruit behaviors fast.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Coin flips made guards and prisoners; days made abusers and breakdowns. Situations cast faster than characters audition — the study's bleak casting call.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Roles recruit behaviors within days.
Coin flips cast crueler than auditions.
Basements plus uniforms produce guards.
Situations direct; characters improvise.

puzzles.title: The Honest Sum
puzzles.question: The matchstick equation reads '6 + 3 = 9'. What is the minimum number of matches to move to make it true?
puzzles.correctExplanation: No moves needed — 6 + 3 genuinely equals 9. Not every matchstick puzzle is broken; checking precedes fixing.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no moves needed. Verify first: 6 + 3 = 9 holds exactly. The puzzle tests whether you audit before operating.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Audit before operating, always.
True equations need zero surgery.
Verification precedes all repairs.
Honest sums ask for hands off.

puzzles.title: The Off-by-Two
puzzles.question: '8 − 3 = 3' is false in matches. Move exactly one matchstick to make a true equation. Which results?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 8 − 3 = 5 — relocate one match within the result digit (3 becomes 5). Internal moves count fully.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 8 − 3 = 5. Reshape the result's 3 into a 5 by moving one segment; 8 − 3 = 5 holds. Internal digit surgery is still one move.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Internal digit surgery counts as one move.
Reshape results before rebuilding operands.
3-to-5 is the classic single relocation.
Small edits fix off-by-two errors.

puzzles.title: The Legion Proof
puzzles.question: The Roman sticks 'VII − II = V' appear in a Latin textbook exercise asking students to find the error. How many sticks are misplaced?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Zero moves — VII minus II genuinely equals V (7 − 2 = 5). Roman arithmetic holds without touching a stick.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is zero moves needed. Decode first: 7 − 2 = 5 is exactly true. Legions demand translation before surgery.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Decode Roman numerals before operating.
True statements need zero surgery.
Translation precedes all repairs here.
Legions hold without touching sticks.

puzzles.title: The Five Dilemma
puzzles.question: A locked box opens only for true equations. Its stick display shows '5 + 5 = 5'. Relocating a single match, which true statement frees the lock?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 6 − 5 = 1 — lift the upright from the plus (making minus) onto the first 5 (making 6). Operator and operand change in one relocation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 6 − 5 = 1. Move the plus's upright bar onto the first 5: plus becomes minus, 5 becomes 6, and 6 − 5 = 1 holds. One match, two transformations.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Operators donate matches to operands.
Plus-to-minus frees exactly one bar.
One relocation can transform twice.
5-to-6 needs a single upright.

puzzles.title: The Added Three
puzzles.question: Maya's puzzle page shows the sticks '8 + 3 = 5'. She may shift exactly one match. Which corrected line earns full marks?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 6 + 3 = 9 — strip the upper-right match from 8 (making 6) and lay it on the result 5 (making 9). Donor and recipient balance exactly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 6 + 3 = 9. The 8 donates one segment to become 6; the result 5 receives it to become 9. Track donors and recipients; arithmetic follows.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Donors and recipients balance exactly.
Strip-and-lay is the core relocation.
8-to-6 frees what 5-to-9 needs.
Track both ends of every moved match.

puzzles.title: The Borrowed Bar
puzzles.question: On a rainy afternoon Tom lays out '6 + 4 = 4' and wagers he can repair it by moving one stick. Which result wins his bet?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 8 − 4 = 4 — borrow the plus's upright for the 6 (making 8) while plus becomes minus. Operator funds operand, equation balances.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 8 − 4 = 4. The plus lends its upright bar to the 6 (making 8) and degrades to minus: 8 − 4 = 4 holds. Borrowed bars balance books.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Plus bars fund neighboring digits.
Borrowed bars balance whole books.
Minus results from generous operators.
6-to-8 needs a single upright.

puzzles.title: The Double Duty
