puzzles.lessonContent:
Integrity compounds like interest steadily.
Betrayals liquidate built capital fast.
Counterparties remember beyond payoffs.
Trust is kept promises capitalized.
Share this: bank one kept promise.

puzzles.title: The Open Grab
puzzles.question: Variant revisited: B lies visibly full at $1M, and every theory — evidential and causal alike — now points the same way. What do they jointly recommend?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Both boxes — with B visibly full, evidence and causation converge: take everything. Unanimous theories end the paradox.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is both boxes. Visible millions align news value with levers: evidentialists see testified riches, causalists see grabbable cash. Convergence dissolves dilemmas.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Visible riches align rival theories.
Convergence dissolves manufactured dilemmas.
News plus levers point together here.
Unanimity ends paradoxes cleanly.
Share this: take one unanimous win.

puzzles.title: The Million's Key
puzzles.question: Strip away theory: empirically, full boxes await exactly those the predictor foresaw restraining themselves. What forecast fills B?
puzzles.correctExplanation: A one-box forecast — fullness follows foresight of restraint, mechanically. Keys are predictions, locks are boxes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a one-box forecast. Track records show millions trailing predicted restraint like shadows. Empirics first: forecasts fill, restraint collects.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Forecasts fill; restraint collects reliably.
Keys are predictions, locks are boxes.
Empirics precede theories in cash matters.
Shadows of restraint carry millions.
Share this: earn one forecast fortune.

puzzles.title: The Knight's Leap
puzzles.question: Abraham raises the knife over Isaac at God's command — murder by every universal ethic, faith by Kierkegaard's. What does the leap of faith suspend?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The universal's claims — teleological suspension: the single individual stands higher than the general for a higher telos. Ethics relativized, not abolished.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the universal claims of ethics. God, feelings, and physics miss it: Abraham keeps faith while breaking morality's universality. Suspension elevates the single above the general paradoxically.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Singles can stand above generals paradoxically.
Suspension elevates; it never abolishes.
Higher telos relativizes universal claims.
Faith begins where ethics ends, terrifyingly.
Share this: feel one paradox's weight today.

puzzles.title: The Double Movement
puzzles.question: The knight of infinite resignation renounces the finite nobly; the knight of faith makes a second movement — receiving finitude back by virtue of the absurd. What distinguishes faith from resignation?
choices: The second movement of joyful reception
puzzles.correctAnswer: The second movement of joyful reception
puzzles.correctExplanation: Joyful reception back — resignation stops at renunciation; faith proceeds to receive the finite again, absurdly. Princes and tax collectors dance while philosophers only renounce.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the second movement of joyful reception. Knowledge, testimony, and age miss it: both knights renounce, only one receives. Faith's extra step looks exactly like bourgeois contentment — invisibly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Receiving back exceeds renouncing nobly.
Second movements hide inside ordinary joy.
Resignation stops; faith proceeds absurdly.
Invisible crowns beat visible sackcloth.
Share this: receive one finite joy absurdly.

puzzles.title: The Inward Truth
puzzles.question: 'Truth is subjectivity' — Kierkegaard locates religious truth in passionate inward appropriation, not detached approximation. What decides truth here?
choices: How passionately the self holds it
puzzles.correctAnswer: How passionately the self holds it
puzzles.correctExplanation: Passionate holding — inwardness decides where objectivity abstains. Faith's truth lives in the how of holding, never the what of content.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is how passionately the self holds it. Consensus, antiquity, and proofs measure objective approximations; faith demands subjective appropriation. The knower's posture constitutes the known.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Postures constitute what they hold.
Holding-how outweighs content-what in faith.
Approximation abstains where passion decides.
Inwardness is truth's religious mode.
Share this: hold one thing passionately.

puzzles.title: The Uncertain Fire
puzzles.question: Faith, Kierkegaard says, holds fast with maximum passion precisely where objective certainty is minimal. What ratio defines belief?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Maximum passion, minimum certainty — uncertainty is faith's oxygen, not its enemy. Objective doubts feed subjective fire.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is maximum passion with minimum certainty. Proportional belief describes science; faith inverts the ratio deliberately. Uncertainty fuels what evidence would extinguish.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Uncertainty fuels faith it would starve in science.
Ratios invert between knowing and believing.
Doubts feed fires they threaten elsewhere.
Passion peaks where proof runs dry.
Share this: burn brightly past evidence once.

puzzles.title: The Seducer's Rotation
puzzles.question: The aesthete survives boredom by 'rotation of crops' — varying soil, not harvesting meaning. Don Juan serializes pleasures to dodge emptiness. What strategy is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Systematic novelty — crop rotation for the soul: change fields, never farm. Boredom managed, meaning never met.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is systematic novelty against boredom. Commitment, devotion, and revolution miss the aesthetic: variety without depth, motion without arrival. Rotation postpones the despair it cannot cure.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Variety postpones despairs it cannot cure.
Motion differs from arrival entirely.
Rotation manages what commitment would heal.
Novelty systems defend against depth.
Share this: farm one field deeply today.

puzzles.title: The Married Judge
puzzles.question: Judge William defends marriage, vocation, and continuity against aesthetic flightiness — choosing oneself through commitment. What stage does he voice?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The ethical — commitment, continuity, choosing the self one already is. Marriage as metaphysics: repetition with meaning.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the ethical stage. Aesthetic flees, religious transcends, irony observes — the Judge commits. Vocation and wedding ring outrank infinite possibility here.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Commitment outranks possibility ethically.
Continuity dignifies repetition with meaning.
Choosing oneself beats sampling selves.
Rings outweigh rotations in this stage.
Share this: choose one continuity today.

puzzles.title: The Suffering Saint
puzzles.question: Beyond ethics lies the religious: Job's suffering, Abraham's paradox — God relating where reason resigns. What marks this highest stage?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Paradoxical God-relation — suffering and absurdity as meeting places. Reason resigns; faith relates anyway.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is paradoxical relation to the absolute. Morals, wealth, and applause belong to lower stages: religion begins where ethics breaks. Job suffers, Abraham lifts knives — both relate past reason.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Religion begins where ethics breaks down.
Suffering becomes meeting place, not problem.
Absurdity hosts what reason cannot.
Relate past understanding's border.
Share this: relate past one border.

puzzles.title: The Fatal Imbalance
puzzles.question: Despair, in The Sickness Unto Death, is misrelation in the self's synthesis — finite/infinite, temporal/eternal, freedom/necessity out of joint. What is despair structurally?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Misrelated synthesis — the self unbalanced across its constitutive polarities. Despair is architecture, not accident.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a misrelated synthesis of opposites. Chemicals, punishments, and genes miss the structure: selves are syntheses, and syntheses can mistune. Diagnose architecture before chemistry.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Selves are syntheses that can mistune.
Polarities need balancing, not amputating.
Architecture precedes chemistry in despair.
Diagnose structures before prescribing pills.
Share this: tune one polarity today.

puzzles.title: The Relating Relation
puzzles.question: 'The self is a relation that relates itself to itself' — a synthesis conscious of synthesizing. What makes human selfhood unique here?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Self-conscious synthesis — relating to one's own relating: spirit as reflexive loop. Bodies, deeds, and grammar miss the reflexive core.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is self-conscious synthesis of opposites. The formula's third term (relating-to-relating) makes spirit: finite-infinite syntheses aware of themselves. Loops, not lumps, define selves.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Loops define selves; lumps merely occupy.
Relating-to-relating makes spirit happen.
Reflexivity crowns synthesis with selfhood.
Third terms transform pairs into persons.
Share this: relate to one relating.

puzzles.title: The Finite Fever
puzzles.question: Despair of finitude lacks infinitude — drowning in facts, deadlines, probabilities, 'the probable' as prison. What does this despair miss?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Possibility beyond calculation — finitude despair suffocates in probable actualities. Facts need windows, not just walls.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the infinite: possibility beyond calculation. Information, schedules, and willpower feed the prison: more facts fatten finitude. Despair of finitude needs air, not data.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Facts fatten finitude's prison daily.
Possibility airs what probability seals.
Windows beat walls for despairing minds.
Calculate less; imagine more.
Share this: open one impossible window.

puzzles.title: The Infinite Drift
puzzles.question: Despair of infinitude lacks finitude — fantasies, feelings, and abstractions with no actuality to anchor them. What does this despair need?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Finitude — limits, decisions, actual mornings. Infinite drift needs ballast, not bigger sails.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is finitude: actuality, limits, decisions. Visions, intensities, and sittings feed the drift: abstraction unmoored is despair's other wing. Anchor in actuality to fly at all.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Abstraction unmoored is despair's wing.
Ballast precedes flight always.
Decisions anchor drifting infinities.
Actual mornings ground possible ones.
Share this: decide one actual thing.

puzzles.title: The Unknowing Sick
puzzles.question: The worst despair, Kierkegaard says, is being unaware of being in despair — spiritlessness mistaking itself for health. What makes it worst?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Unawareness — unfelt sickness seeks no cure: the spiritless call it realism. Conscious despair at least knows its address.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is its unawareness of itself. Symptoms, rarity, and noise miss it: unknown illness never consults doctors. Spiritlessness posing as health is despair's perfect camouflage.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Unknown illnesses never seek cures.
Camouflage perfects what pain would expose.
Realism poses mask spiritlessness often.
Consciousness, even pained, beats numbness.
Share this: check one numbness honestly.

puzzles.title: The Crowd Verdict
puzzles.question: 'The crowd is untruth' — Kierkegaard insists truth needs the single individual; majorities decide nothing about the eternal. Where does truth reside?
puzzles.correctExplanation: With the single individual — crowds vote on matters where voting is nonsense. Eternal questions need solitary deciders.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is with the single individual. Majorities, institutions, and volumes miss it: truth doesn't poll well. One person can be right against ten thousand — categorically.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Polls malfunction on eternal questions.
Solitary deciders carry truth sometimes.
Majorities decide nothing ultimate ever.
One against ten thousand can win truly.
Share this: stand singly once today.

puzzles.title: The Leveling Press
puzzles.question: The daily press, Kierkegaard warned, levels all excellence into equally consumable chatter — no one may stand out. What does leveling destroy?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Distinction itself — leveling makes eminence unreadable: all flattened to audience level. Chatter consumes what admiration would crown.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is distinction itself. Profits, literacy, and post miss it: the press's leveling abstraction dissolves qualitatively different into quantitatively same. Excellence becomes content.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Abstractions dissolve qualitative differences.
Content flattens what admiration crowned.
Leveling reads eminence as noise.
Distinction needs defenders, not just admirers.
Share this: admire one distinction fully.

puzzles.title: The Passionless Age
puzzles.question: The present age, Kierkegaard charged, is reflective and passionless — all deliberation, no enthusiasm, envy as its only unity. What characterizes it?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Reflection without passion — thinking that never bleeds into action. Deliberation replaces devotion; envy replaces admiration.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reflection without passion. Fervor, labor, and crowds miss it: the age thinks everything and does nothing. Passionless reflection is the specific modern sickness.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Thinking-that-never-bleeds sickens ages.
Deliberation replaces devotion silently.
Envy unites where admiration divided.
Passionlessness is the precise diagnosis.
Share this: bleed into one action today.

puzzles.title: The Envious Glue
puzzles.question: In passionless ages, Kierkegaard says, envy becomes the negative unifying principle — all secretly level all. What binds such societies?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Mutual envy — secret leveling pacts: none shall rise, all shall watch. Negative unity binds tighter than positive.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is mutual envy. Admiration, worship, and enterprise unite positively; envy unites by shared resentment of eminence. Glue made of grievance holds firmest.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Grievance glues firmer than admiration.
Leveling pacts bind secretly always.
Negative unity outlasts positive easily.
Envy organizes where love disperses.
Share this: admire instead of envying once.

puzzles.title: The Midwife Method
puzzles.question: Truth that concerns existing — how to live — cannot be taught directly but must be midwifed: the learner gives birth herself. What communication does this require?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Indirect maieutic communication — Socratic midwifery for existential truth. Direct teaching delivers information; only indirection delivers transformation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is indirect, maieutic communication. Lectures inform, repetitions drill, exams test — none beget. Existing-truths need birthing assistance, never prefab delivery.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Birthing beats delivering for living truths.
Midwives assist; lecturers merely inform.
Indirection respects learner inwardness.
Prefab truths transform nobody ever.
Share this: midwife one insight today.

puzzles.title: The Dizzy Edge
puzzles.question: Anxiety, Kierkegaard writes, is 'the dizziness of freedom' — staring into possibility's abyss where one can choose. What causes this vertigo?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Possibility's abyss — freedom vertiginizes because everything might be chosen. Dizziness measures openness, not altitude.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is freedom's abyss of possibility. Cliffs, sugar, and sleep miss it: the precipice is internal — 'I can' stretching infinitely. Vertigo gauges freedom's depth precisely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Openness vertiginizes more than heights.
'I can' stretches infinitely inward.
Dizziness gauges freedom's depth well.
Abysses internal dwarf external ones.
Share this: peer into one possibility.

puzzles.title: The Necessary Offense
puzzles.question: The God-man paradox necessarily offends reason — offense isn't a bug but the mark of encountering transcendence. What does offense signal?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Genuine paradox-encounter — offense is reason's correct response to the absurd. Smooth doctrines never touched transcendence.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is genuine encounter with paradox. Falsity, preaching, and translation miss it: offense certifies contact with what exceeds understanding. The unoffended never met the paradox.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Offense certifies transcendent contact.
Smoothness signals absence of paradox.
Reason rightly chokes on infinity.
Unoffended means unencountered here.
Share this: be offended productively once.

puzzles.title: The Doubled Return
puzzles.question: Job loses everything, then receives everything back doubled — not recollection of the past but repetition forward. What does genuine repetition give?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The same made new — repetition isn't recollection backward but reception forward: Job's doubled goods are new gifts, not returned loans.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the same goods made new. Restoration, nostalgia, and compensation miss it: repetition moves forward where recollection looks back. Doubled returns are new creations.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Forward reception beats backward recollection.
New gifts differ from returned loans.
Doubling signifies creation, not refund.
Repeat forward, never merely recall.
Share this: receive one return as new.

puzzles.title: The Patient Soul
puzzles.question: 'In patience you will gain your souls' — Kierkegaard reads patience not as passive waiting but as active soul-winning. What does patience gain?
puzzles.correctExplanation: One's soul itself — patience as self-acquisition: enduring time without fleeing it wins the endurer. Waiting works when waiting wills.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is one's soul itself. Rewards, approval, and power miss it: patience gains the waiter, not the waited-for. Soul-winning happens in duration endured.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Waiting wills what fleeing forfeits.
Duration endured wins endurers.
Souls gained through patience kept.
Active waiting beats passive killing-time.
Share this: gain one minute soulfully.

puzzles.title: The Knowing Ignorance
puzzles.question: Socrates claimed wisdom in knowing that he knew nothing, while sophists professed omniscience. What makes ignorance philosophical?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Awareness of not knowing — examined ignorance opens inquiry where professed knowledge closes it. Socratic wisdom is meta-knowing.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is awareness of not knowing. Skepticism denies, doctrines stockpile, debates perform — only owned ignorance inquires. Sophists knew everything and learned nothing.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Owned ignorance inquires; professed knowledge rests.
Meta-knowing beats knowing in philosophy.
Sophists stockpile; Socrates empties usefully.
Examinations begin with confessed gaps.
Share this: confess one fertile ignorance.

puzzles.title: The Silent Knight
puzzles.question: Agamemnon can speechify his sacrifice; Abraham must stay silent — faith speaks no universal tongue. What can the knight of faith never do?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Speak his justification aloud — ethics demands communicability; faith transcends it. Silence is the paradox's native tongue.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is speak his justification aloud. Anguish felt, commands obeyed, love intact — yet no universal words exist for the act. Tragic heroes explain; knights of faith cannot.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Universals demand speech; paradoxes forbid it.
Silence is faith's native tongue here.
Tragic heroes explain; knights cannot.
Incommunicability marks transcendence exactly.
Share this: keep one silence faithfully.

puzzles.title: The Chosen Choice
puzzles.question: Either/Or's deepest choice isn't pleasure versus duty but choosing versus drifting — willing to will at all. What comes before every option?
puzzles.correctExplanation: To choose at all — meta-choice precedes content: drifters never reach options. Willing to will is freedom's first act.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is to choose at all. Pleasures, wealth, and youth are contents; choosing is the container. Aesthetes drift among options they never elect.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Containers precede contents in freedom.
Drifters never reach real options.
Willing-to-will is freedom's first act.
Meta-choices govern all object choices.
Share this: elect one option deliberately.

puzzles.title: The Fixed Cage
puzzles.question: One despair insists everything is necessary — nothing can be otherwise, effort is theater. Against such fatalism, what is missing?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Possibility — necessity-everywhere is mood posing as metaphysics. Denied openings remain open regardless.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is possibility. Effort-theater excuses surrender in advance; fatalism mistakes feeling for fact. Openings denied are openings still.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Necessity claimed everywhere suffocates action.
Theater-effort beliefs excuse all surrender.
Openings denied are openings still.
Fatalism mistakes mood for metaphysics.
Share this: open one denied maybe today.

puzzles.title: The Counting Blindness
puzzles.question: Volunteers counting basketball passes famously miss a person in a gorilla suit strolling through the game. What walks past focused counters unseen?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The gorilla — focused counting burns the attention needed to notice it. Looking never equals seeing.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the gorilla. Pass-counting consumes the attentional budget entirely; an obvious intruder crosses unseen. Sustained focus blinds peripheries absolutely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Sustained focus blinds peripheries absolutely.
Counting consumes whole attentional budgets.
Looking never equals seeing anything.
Obvious intruders cross unseen routinely.
Share this: count passes and miss everything.

puzzles.title: The Door Swap
puzzles.question: A stranger asking directions is briefly blocked by a carried door — and a different person continues the conversation. Most pedestrians never notice. What escapes them?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The switch — change blindness: visual details of strangers never encode. Conversations continue with replacements unnoticed.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the switch. Door-study pedestrians fail to detect a changed interlocutor because faces of strangers encode thinly. Memory stores gist, never mugshots.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Stranger faces encode thinly at best.
Gist memory skips identifying details.
Doors swap people unnoticed daily.
Conversations continue past substitutions.
Share this: describe one stranger precisely.

puzzles.title: The Jam Defense
puzzles.question: Shoppers choosing jams are secretly handed their rejected jar — then fluently justify preferring it. What manipulation goes undetected?
puzzles.correctExplanation: The swap — choice blindness: decisions unmonitored, justifications improvised. Preferences narrated after the fact.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the swap. Johansson's shoppers defend jams they rejected seconds earlier: choice monitoring is theater, confabulation the understudy. Reasons follow choices, rarely lead.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Reasons follow choices more than lead.
Confabulation understudies every decision.
Monitoring is theater; narrative improvises.
Defended picks may never have been picked.
Share this: defend one unchosen jam.

puzzles.title: The Expert Blindness
puzzles.question: Expert radiologists hunting nodules miss a drawn gorilla on CT scans; novice counters miss costumed intruders. What single phenomenon covers both failures?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Inattentional blindness — expertise upgrades targets, never attention itself. Focused tasks blind all ranks equally.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is inattentional blindness. Nodule-hunters and pass-counters share one bottleneck: attended tasks consume seeing. Expertise changes what, never whether, focus blinds.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Expertise upgrades targets, never attention.
Bottlenecks blind all ranks equally.
Focused tasks consume seeing itself.
What-focus differs; blindness persists.
Share this: miss one obvious gorilla.

puzzles.title: The Name Beacon
puzzles.question: Shadowing speech in one ear, listeners ignore the other channel entirely — except for one stimulus that always breaks through. What pierces the block?
puzzles.correctExplanation: One's own name — the cocktail-party beacon: self-relevance pierces inattention automatically. Identity monitors all channels at once.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is one's own name. Cherry's shadowers miss language switches yet catch their names: a background watchman screens everything for self. Attention has a permanent back door.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Identity monitors all channels at once.
Self-relevance pierces every block automatically.
Background watchmen screen for selfhood.
Names are permanent back doors.
Share this: whisper one name across noise.

puzzles.title: The Fading Watch
puzzles.question: Radar operators miss steadily more signals as shifts drag on — attention itself tires like a muscle. What fades with time on task?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Vigilance — sustained attention decrements measurably within half an hour. Watches tire faster than eyes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is vigilance. Mackworth's clock-watchers proved attention fades as a function of time alone: signals missed multiply across shifts. Muscles tire; so does monitoring.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Monitoring tires like muscles do.
Signals missed multiply across shifts.
Time-on-task degrades detection steadily.
Watches need relief, never willpower.
Share this: relieve one watch early.

puzzles.title: The Wandering Half
puzzles.question: Experience-sampling finds minds stray from the present task nearly half of waking life. What occupies this enormous share?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Mind-wandering — nearly half of consciousness runs off-task: planning, replaying, imagining. Presence is the minority report.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mind-wandering. Killingsworth's pings caught stray thought around 47% of hours: humans live largely elsewhere. Unhappiness tracks wandering, not location.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Presence is consciousness's minority report.
Stray thought fills nearly half of hours.
Wandering predicts unhappiness better than location.
Elsewhere is the default address.
Share this: catch one wandering episode.

puzzles.title: The Skipped Banner
puzzles.question: Web users automatically skip page regions shaped like advertisements — regardless of actual content placed there. What gets ignored by shape alone?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Banner areas — shape-learned skipping: ad-geometry means do-not-read. Content dies at the border of learned blindness.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is banner areas. Eye-tracking shows learned avoidance of ad-shaped zones whatever they hold. Geometry triggers skipping before content loads.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Geometries trigger skipping pre-content.
Learned avoidance outruns reading entirely.
Shapes mean do-not-read reliably.
Borders kill content before loading.
Share this: read one banner-shaped box.

puzzles.title: The Threshold Forgetting
puzzles.question: Walking through doorways measurably impairs recall of intentions formed in the previous room. What does crossing thresholds disrupt?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Doorway effect — event boundaries flush working memory: new rooms, new files. Intentions die at thresholds routinely.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is doorway effect. Radvansky's walkers forget errands upon room change: boundaries segment experience and dump buffers. Architecture edits memory silently.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Boundaries segment experience silently.
New rooms open new mental files.
Buffers dump at every threshold.
Architecture edits memory constantly.
Share this: blame one doorway aloud.

puzzles.title: The Hands-Free Myth
puzzles.question: Hands-free phone calls impair driving about as badly as drunk driving. With hands free and eyes forward, what stays impaired?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Driver attention — conversation consumes the mind, not the hands. Eyes forward, mind elsewhere: inattention blindness at speed.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is driver attention. Strayer's simulators prove hands-free parity with intoxication: cognitive load, not manual load, kills. Forward eyes never guarantee present minds.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Cognitive load kills regardless of hands.
Forward eyes hide absent minds.
Conversation consumes driving attention.
Hands-free never means brain-free.
Share this: hang up before driving once.

puzzles.title: The Fountain Walker
puzzles.question: Phone-distracted pedestrians walk into fountains, poles, and traffic with rising injury counts. What modern hazard has a diagnosis?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Distracted walking — screens capture gaze while streets demand it. Fountains fill with the inattentive annually.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is distracted walking. Emergency rooms code the collisions: eyes down, world unmonitored. Urban furniture defeats divided pedestrians reliably.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Screens capture gaze streets demand.
Divided pedestrians lose to furniture.
Down-eyes forfeit right-of-way awareness.
Fountains collect the inattentive yearly.
Share this: pocket one phone per block.

puzzles.title: The Gun Memory
puzzles.question: Robbery witnesses recall the weapon vividly but the face barely at all. What steals face memory during crimes?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Weapon focus — threat captures the attentional bottleneck, starving face encoding. Guns photograph; faces blur.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is weapon focus. Eyes lock threat while faces pass unencoded: attention is zero-sum under fear. Testimony remembers steel, forgets features.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Threats monopolize encoding bandwidth.
Zero-sum attention starves faces for guns.
Fear photographs weapons, blurs people.
Bottlenecks pick threats over identities.
Share this: notice one face fully today.

puzzles.title: The Tired Monitor
puzzles.question: CCTV operators watching wall-to-wall screens miss incidents that later footage shows plainly. What fatigues across multi-screen shifts?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Monitoring fatigue — sustained divided watching degrades exactly like radar duty. Walls of screens exhaust faster than single views.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is monitoring fatigue. More screens multiply load, not coverage: attention thins across displays until incidents pass unseen. Coverage promised exceeds attention delivered.
puzzles.lessonContent:
More screens multiply load, not coverage.
Divided watching thins to transparency.
Promised coverage exceeds delivered attention.
Walls exhaust faster than windows.
Share this: watch one screen truly.

puzzles.title: The Stubborn Word
puzzles.question: Naming ink colors while ignoring the color words themselves (RED in blue ink) slows everyone measurably. What captures attention against orders?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Stroop interference — reading runs automatically and collides with color-naming. Literacy hijacks intention effortlessly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is Stroop interference. Word meanings barge in uninvited: suppressing reading costs time every trial. Automaticity overrules orders reliably.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Automaticity overrules orders reliably.
Reading barges in uninvited always.
Suppression costs time every trial.
Literacy hijacks color intentions.
Share this: fail one Stroop test proudly.

puzzles.title: The Blink Gap
puzzles.question: In rapid image streams, viewers spotting a first target miss a second landing a fraction of a second later. What blanks the follow-up?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Attentional blink — processing the first target occupies the bottleneck for ~half a second. Seconds in streams vanish during encoding.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is attentional blink. RSVP experiments prove encoding blocks follow-ups for hundreds of milliseconds: attention blinks after each catch. Streams outrun bottlenecks routinely.

puzzles.title: The Dismissed Prophet
puzzles.question: Cursed to prophesy truly and never be believed, I watch Troy burn exactly as foretold. Priests dismiss me; fires vindicate me. Who am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Cassandra — truly prophesying, never believed, vindicated by flames. Apollo's gift wrapped in curse.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is Cassandra. True-foretold plus never-believed plus Troy-burned isolates the cursed prophetess: gift and curse in one utterance. Fires review what priests rejected.
puzzles.hintText:
True prophecies earn me dismissal.
Troy burns exactly as I foretold.
Priests wave away my warnings.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Gifts wrapped in curses confuse all.
Fires review rejected warnings finally.
True foretelling earns dismissal often.
Curses hide inside blessings here.
Share this: heed one dismissed voice.

puzzles.title: The Sought Absence
puzzles.question: Seek me and I retreat; surrender the search and I arrive. Losing the little self finds the boundless one. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Enlightenment — retreating from seekers, arriving for surrenderers. The found is the unfound-by-trying.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is enlightenment. Seek-retreats plus surrender-arrives isolates awakening's paradox: grasping hands close around air. Boundlessness admits the selfless only.
puzzles.hintText:
Seeking repels my arrival daily.
Surrender summons what chasing scatters.
Little selves block boundless ones.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Grasping closes around air always.
Surrender summons what chasing scatters.
Boundlessness admits selfless seekers.
Unfound-by-trying defines arrival.
Share this: surrender one search today.

puzzles.title: The Oldest Newborn
puzzles.question: I am the oldest day you'll never see again and the newest you will ever have. Yesterday envies me; tomorrow borrows from me. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Today — oldest in passing, newest in having. The hinge day envied behind and borrowed ahead.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is today. Oldest-never-again plus newest-ever-had isolates the present hinge: behind envies, ahead borrows. Days pivot on this one.
puzzles.hintText:
Never-seen-again meets never-had-yet.
Yesterday envies my position.
Tomorrow borrows all my hours.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hinges pivot pasts and futures.
Behind envies; ahead borrows constantly.
Oldest passing meets newest having.
Pivot days deserve full presence.
Share this: inhabit one hinge fully.

puzzles.title: The False Memory
puzzles.question: I feel exactly like remembering something that never happened; travelers know me in streets they've never walked. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Déjà vu — familiarity without history, recognition without source. Memory's misfire feels like its function.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is déjà vu. Unwalked-familiar plus never-happened-remembered isolates false recognition: glitch or signal, science still debates. Feeling certain proves nothing here.
puzzles.hintText:
Unwalked streets feel well-trodden.
Never-happened feels remembered.
Travelers meet me most often.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Familiarity without history misleads.
Recognition needs sources to trust.
Glitches mimic functions perfectly.
Certainty proves nothing alone.
Share this: doubt one familiarity.

puzzles.title: The Tongueless Choir
puzzles.question: No tongue, yet every nation understands; no lessons needed where I play. What needs no translation?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Music — tongueless choir understood worldwide. Phrases beyond all grammars.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is music. No-tongue plus every-nation plus no-lessons isolates the universal art: grammars divide, melodies unite. Translation dies where music speaks.
puzzles.hintText:
Nations understand without lessons.
Tongues never shape my phrases.
Translation is meaningless to me.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Melodies unite where grammars divide.
Universal arts need no tongues.
Lessons unnecessary mark true universals.
Phrases beyond grammar persuade all.
Share this: hum one universal tonight.

puzzles.title: The Loud Quiet
puzzles.question: I fill rooms the moment conversation dies; hosts dread my arrival while philosophers praise my honesty. What am I?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Awkward silence — filling dead conversation, dreaded by hosts, praised by philosophers. Emptiness with volume.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is awkward silence. Conversation-dies-arrives plus hosts-dread plus thinkers-praise isolates social quiet: honesty too loud for comfort. Volumes of nothing deafen politely.
puzzles.hintText:
Dying talk summons me instantly.
Hosts dread what thinkers praise.
Rooms fill with my emptiness.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Honesty too loud discomforts politely.
Dead talk summons full emptiness.
Dreaded by hosts, praised by sages.
Volumes of nothing deafen rooms.
Share this: endure one loud quiet.

puzzles.title: The Spreading Truth
puzzles.question: Textbooks call entropy 'disorder' — teenagers picture messy bedrooms. Physicists increasingly teach it as energy spreading out. What does entropy actually track?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Energy spreading across microstates — disorder metaphors mislead (a tidy crystal can hold more entropy than slush). Spreading, not messiness, is the quantity.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is energy spreading across microstates. Eyes, dishes, and morals miss it: entropy counts energetic arrangements, and tidy ice can outrank messy water. Bedrooms mislead thermodynamics.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Metaphors mislead where quantities clarify.
Spreading, never messiness, is tracked.
Tidy crystals can outrank slushy melts.
Bedrooms are terrible thermodynamic models.
Share this: retire one disorder metaphor.

puzzles.title: The Open Kitchen
puzzles.question: Creationists argue evolution violates the second law (order from chaos). Earth, however, bathes in solar influx while radiating waste heat. Why is there no violation?
choices: The second law applies only to isolated systems
puzzles.correctAnswer: The second law applies only to isolated systems
puzzles.correctExplanation: Only isolated systems — Earth trades energy with space: low-entropy sunlight in, high-entropy heat out. Local order paid by solar income.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the second law applies only to isolated systems. Law-breaking, pauses, and exemptions miss it: open systems order themselves on through-flows. Life is a solar-powered eddy, fully lawful.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Open systems order on through-flows lawfully.
Isolation scopes the second law strictly.
Solar income funds biological complexity.
Eddies obey rivers they ride within.
Share this: audit one open system.

puzzles.title: The Costly Meal
puzzles.question: Schrödinger said life feeds on 'negative entropy' — importing order to stave off decay. Every meal, at bottom, imports what?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Low-entropy arrangement — food's value is structural order organisms dismantle for work. Calories count energy; arrangement counts usefulness.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is low-entropy arrangement. Heat, morals, and water miss it: bodies harvest molecular order, excreting disorder as heat and waste. Eating is entropy arbitrage.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Bodies harvest order, excrete disorder.
Arrangement counts beyond calories.
Entropy arbitrage funds all living.
Order imported staves decay daily.
Share this: eat one negentropy lunch.

puzzles.title: The Final Equilibrium
puzzles.question: Cosmology's heat death pictures a universe expanded into uniform lukewarm equilibrium. What ends when gradients vanish?
puzzles.correctExplanation: All change, work, and life — gradients drive everything; equilibrium drives nothing. The end is boredom, not bang.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is all change, work, and life. Matter persists, gravity holds, time flows — but nothing happens anywhere. Difference, not substance, is existence's fuel.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Gradients drive; equilibrium idles forever.
Difference fuels existence, not substance.
Boredom, not bang, ends universes.
Work needs slopes of every kind.
Share this: cherish one gradient today.

puzzles.title: The Unrecyclable Remainder
puzzles.question: Enthusiasts promise fully circular economies, but thermodynamics mandates losses: dissipation, mixing, contamination. What can recycling never fully defeat?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Entropy's toll — every cycle scatters some material beyond economic recovery. Circularity approaches but never arrives.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is entropy's dissipative toll. Greed, laziness, and bins miss it: physics taxes each loop with dispersion. Perfect circles violate the second law's economics.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Physics taxes every loop with losses.
Dispersion defeats perfect circularity.
Approach circles; never promise them.
Tolls apply regardless of virtue.
Share this: trace one dissipative loss.

puzzles.title: The Energy Ledger
puzzles.question: Energy Return on Investment divides energy delivered by energy spent getting it. Early oil returned ~100:1; modern sources return far less. What does falling EROI mean?
choices: More effort per unit of useful energy
puzzles.correctAnswer: More effort per unit of useful energy
puzzles.correctExplanation: More effort per useful unit — civilization runs on surplus energy, and shrinking surpluses squeeze everything built atop them. Net energy, not gross, powers societies.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is more effort per unit of useful energy. Profits, chemistry, and sunlight miss it: EROI measures physical surplus before economics. Societies spend net, never gross.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Net energy powers societies, never gross.
Surpluses squeezed strain everything atop.
Physical returns precede economic ones.
Ledger energy before pricing it.
Share this: compute one EROI roughly.

puzzles.title: The Coal Paradox
puzzles.question: Efficient steam engines were meant to save coal; coal use soared instead, as cheaper power multiplied uses. What paradox is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Efficiency raising total consumption — Jevons paradox: cheaper steam expanded applications faster than savings accumulated. Frugality per unit, profligacy in total.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is efficiency raising total consumption. Breakdowns, celebrations, and discoveries miss it: falling costs grow demand beyond engineering savings. Economies rebound past engineers' arithmetic.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Falling costs grow demand past savings.
Frugality per unit, profligacy in total.
Rebounds outrun engineering arithmetic.
Efficiency needs caps to save anything.
Share this: spot one Jevons rebound.

puzzles.title: The Driven Miles
puzzles.question: Fuel-efficient cars get driven extra miles, clawing back part of the engineering savings. What is this take-back called?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Direct rebound — cheaper miles invite more miles: 10-30% of savings typically return as driving. Efficiency leaks through behavior.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is direct rebound effect. Failures, tires, and taxes miss it: per-mile savings fund extra miles directly. Engineering gains share proceeds with behavior.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Per-mile savings fund extra miles.
Behavior shares engineering proceeds.
Take-backs run ten to thirty percent.
Efficiency leaks through use patterns.
Share this: track one rebound of yours.

puzzles.title: The Finite Pie
puzzles.question: Ecological economists argue endless GDP growth on a finite planet collides with material-energy realities. What ultimately constrains perpetual growth?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Material-energy throughput limits — economies metabolize matter and energy; planets supply finite flows. Growth hits physics before imagination.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is material-energy throughput limits. Bankers, ads, and bandwidth miss it: throughput, not money, binds. Dematerialization helps at margins; physics holds the totals.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Throughput binds where money only measures.
Metabolisms need material flows always.
Margins yield; totals obey physics.
Growth meets geology eventually.
Share this: weigh one throughput limit.

puzzles.title: The Exported Smoke
puzzles.question: Factories vent smoke freely while neighbors cough: real costs dumped outside market prices. Economically, what is pollution?
puzzles.correctExplanation: An unpriced entropy export — disorder shipped off-book to shared airs and waters. Prices lie by omission; lungs keep true ledgers.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is an unpriced entropy export. Gifts, strategies, and errors miss it: externalities are thermodynamic dumping with the invoice torn up. Markets optimize the priced and ignore the rest.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Invoices torn up don't cancel costs.
Lungs keep ledgers markets omit.
Disorder shipped off-book returns as harm.
Prices lie most by omission.
Share this: price one externality.

puzzles.title: The Thinning Vein
puzzles.question: Copper ores slid from ~4% metal to under 1%; each ton now demands far more energy and rock moved. What makes modern mining hungrier?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Declining ore grades — rich veins mined first leave lean rock: energy per ton climbs as concentration falls. Geology grades on a curve downward.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is declining ore grades. Laziness, helmets, and lunches miss it: concentration dictates energy cost directly. First fruits were richest; tailings grow leaner.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Concentration dictates energy cost directly.
First fruits run richest always.
Lean rock demands fat energy.
Grades slide; costs climb correspondingly.
Share this: trace one thinning vein.

puzzles.title: The Flow Peak
puzzles.question: 'Peak oil' was misread as running dry; the real crunch is flow rates — how fast wells deliver, not totals underground. What actually peaks?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Extractable flow rate — economies burn flows, not stocks: delivery speed constrains before reserves empty. Peaks are about pace.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is extractable flow rate. Prices, volumes, and careers miss it: civilization drinks from a straw, and straws narrow first. Stocks comfort; flows command.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Straws narrow before wells empty.
Flows command where stocks comfort.
Delivery speed constrains economies first.
Pace peaks precede volume peaks.
Share this: watch one flow narrow.

puzzles.title: The Hundred Millennia
puzzles.question: Some nuclear waste stays dangerous 100,000+ years — longer than writing, cities, or states have existed. What unprecedented problem is this?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Deep-time stewardship — guarding hazards across civilizational timescales no institution has survived. Waste outlives every warden imagined.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is deep-time stewardship. Costs, paint, and flavors miss it: the problem is temporal, not technical — warning beings 3,000 generations hence. Ethics must outlive languages.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Hazards outlive every imagined warden.
Temporal problems dwarf technical ones.
Warnings must cross civilizational gaps.
Stewardship spans a hundred millennia.
Share this: warn one distant descendant.

puzzles.title: The Discounted Future
puzzles.question: Climate economics hinges on discounting: Stern's near-zero pure time preference versus Nordhaus's higher rate moves trillions. What is truly debated?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Discounting future welfare — how much less tomorrow's lives count is ethics disguised as math. Rates are moral philosophy with decimal points.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is discounting future welfare ethically. Brands, forecasts, and dating miss it: pure time preference prices unborn lives. Trillions swing on moral parameters.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Rates are moral philosophy decimalized.
Decimals price unborn lives directly.
Trillions hinge on ethical parameters.
Math disguises morals here completely.
Share this: price one future life.

puzzles.title: The Carbon Purse
puzzles.question: For 1.5°C, humanity may emit only ~400 GtCO₂ more — a finite stock, not a yearly rate that resets. What does the budget frame?
puzzles.correctExplanation: A finite total stock — every ton spends shared purse permanently. Budgets make procrastination visible as spending.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a finite total stock. Variance, bills, and cycles miss it: stocks don't reset January first. Delay spends; the purse notices.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Stocks never reset January first.
Delay spends from shared purses.
Procrastination is visible spending here.
Purses notice what calendars forgive.
Share this: spend one carbon ton mindfully.

puzzles.title: The One-Way Door
puzzles.question: Ice sheets and rainforests may flip past thresholds with no return trip at any price — collapse now, regret forever. What makes these special?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Irreversible thresholds — one-way doors in Earth systems: crossing costs everything, uncrossing costs impossibility. Precaution prices asymmetry.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is irreversible thresholds. Reversibility, cheapness, and fame miss it: some doors lock behind crossers permanently. Asymmetry demands precaution mathematics.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Doors lock behind crossers permanently.
Asymmetry demands precaution math.
Crossing costs everything; return costs impossibility.
One-way systems punish experiments.
Share this: respect one locked door.

puzzles.title: The Costly Kilogram
puzzles.question: Roughly 10% of energy passes each trophic level — a beef kilogram costs many feed kilograms. What does this rule imply for diets?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Meat's thermodynamic costliness — each level taxes 90%: eat low for energetic thrift. Trophic arithmetic favors plants enormously.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is meat's thermodynamic costliness. Taste, labor, and photosynthesis miss it: tenths compound cruelly up food chains. Diets are energy strategies wearing culture.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Tenths compound cruelly up chains.
Low eating is energetic thrift.
Diets strategize energy under culture.
Plants win thermodynamic accounting.
Share this: eat one level lower.

puzzles.title: The Pale Harvest
puzzles.question: Crops convert barely 1-2% of sunlight to biomass — reflection, off-spectrum light, and respiration claim the rest. Why is harvest so thin?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Losses at every step — reflection, spectrum mismatch, photorespiration, maintenance: physics taxes photons repeatedly. Thin harvests are honest accounting.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is losses at every conversion step. Laziness, scarcity, and plots miss it: each transformation keeps its cut. Biomass is what survives the gauntlet.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Gauntlets tax photons repeatedly.
Thin harvests are honest accounting.
Each transformation keeps its cut.
Biomass survives stacked losses.
Share this: thank one surviving photon.

puzzles.title: The Mandatory Waste
puzzles.question: No heat engine beats the Carnot limit fixed by reservoir temperatures. Waste heat isn't poor engineering but what?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Thermodynamic necessity — temperature gaps cap conversion absolutely: some heat must exit. Necessity, not negligence, warms rivers.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is thermodynamic necessity. Unions, materials, and luck miss it: the second law takes its cut from every engine. Perfect conversion is forbidden, not merely difficult.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Second law takes cuts from all engines.
Forbidden differs from difficult entirely.
Necessity warms rivers, not negligence.
Gaps cap conversions absolutely.
Share this: forgive one warm river.

puzzles.title: The Impossible Efficiency
puzzles.question: Heat pumps deliver 3-4 heat units per electricity unit — over 100% 'efficient' without breaking physics. How is this possible?
choices: Moving ambient heat, not making it
puzzles.correctAnswer: Moving ambient heat, not making it
puzzles.correctExplanation: Moving, not making — pumps relocate ambient warmth instead of manufacturing it. Efficiency exceeds 100% because the denominator counts only the moving work.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is moving ambient heat, not making it. Perpetual motion, faulty meters, and secret fuel miss it: relocation beats creation thermodynamically. Pump, don't produce.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Relocation beats creation thermodynamically.
Denominators count moving work only.
Pump ambient; don't manufacture.
Over-100% is bookkeeping, not magic.
Share this: move one unit of warmth.

puzzles.title: The Erasure Price
puzzles.question: Erasing one bit of information costs at least kT ln 2 of energy — computation has a thermodynamic floor. What sets this minimum?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Landauer's limit — forgetting is physical: erased bits heat the universe measurably. Information is thermodynamic currency.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is Landauer's limit. Moore, Metcalfe, and Murphy miss it: erasure dissipates, reversibility excepted. Forgetting costs; computers pay in heat.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Forgetting costs physical currency.
Erased bits heat universes measurably.
Information is thermodynamic throughout.
Floors exist beneath all computing.
Share this: erase one bit reverently.

puzzles.title: The Demon's Ledger
puzzles.question: Maxwell's demon sorts molecules seemingly for free — until physicists billed the measurement itself. What exorcises the demon?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Information's physical cost — knowing which molecule goes where costs entropy that pays the books. Demons starve on honest accounting.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is information has physical cost. Bigger, faster, and larger miss it: measurement and memory are thermodynamic acts. Ledgers balance; demons default.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Knowing costs entropy always.
Measurement is thermodynamic action.
Ledgers balance; demons default.
Honest accounting starves paradoxes.
Share this: price one measurement.

puzzles.title: The Stubborn Sectors
puzzles.question: Aviation, steel, and cement resist electrification — energy density, blast heat, and process chemistry block easy swaps. What makes them hardest?
puzzles.correctExplanation: No easy substitutes — physics, not will, blocks: batteries can't fly far, furnaces need carbon chemistry. Hard sectors need new processes, not pep talks.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no easy physical substitutes. Unions, effort, and PR miss it: constraints are material. Decarbonizing atoms differs from decarbonizing electrons.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Material constraints beat pep talks.
Atoms decarbonize harder than electrons.
Substitutes missing means processes needed.
Physics, not will, blocks hardest.
Share this: respect one hard sector.

puzzles.title: The Mile Myth
puzzles.question: Food miles dominate green-eating debates, yet production method dwarfs transport in most footprints. What matters more than distance traveled?
puzzles.correctExplanation: How it was grown — production dominates footprints: heated greenhouses out-emit field imports. Methods outweigh mileage massively.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is how it was grown. Colors, brands, and shelves miss it: analyses rank production first, transport a distant second. Miles mislead; methods matter.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Production dominates footprints decisively.
Methods outweigh mileage massively.
Greenhouses out-emit imports routinely.
Miles mislead; methods matter.
Share this: grow one awareness.

puzzles.title: The Limestone Debt
puzzles.question: Cement emits CO₂ not just from kiln fuel but from limestone's own chemistry (calcination). Why do these emissions resist fixes?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Chemistry itself releases it — CaCO₃ becomes CaO plus CO₂ by formula, not by fuel choice. Process emissions ignore energy swaps.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is chemistry itself releases CO₂. Workers, paint, and bags miss it: the reaction exhales regardless of heat source. Formulas, not furnaces, set the floor.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Formulas set floors furnaces cannot.
Reactions exhale regardless of fuel.
Process emissions ignore energy swaps.
Chemistry constrains before engineering.
Share this: read one formula's exhaust.

puzzles.title: The Clashing Pair
puzzles.question: Cognitive dissonance theory holds that holding inconsistent beliefs — or acting against beliefs — produces real psychological discomfort.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Inconsistency hurts: minds strain toward coherence, and the strain motivates change. Discomfort is the theory's engine.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Festinger's core claim is affective, not just logical: contradiction feels bad, and feeling bad moves minds. Comfort demands consistency.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Contradiction feels bad before thinking starts.
Strain motivates changes logic cannot.
Coherence comforts more than truth does.
Discomfort engines all dissonance effects.
Share this: notice one clash aching.

puzzles.title: The Dollar Gap
puzzles.question: In Festinger and Carlsmith's classic study, participants paid $1 to lie about a boring task later rated it MORE enjoyable than those paid $20.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Twenty dollars justified lying externally; one dollar forced internal justification — attitude followed. Less pay, more persuasion of self.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The $20 group blamed the money; the $1 group, lacking cover, convinced themselves. Insufficient justification moves attitudes that ample bribes leave parked.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Small rewards move attitudes most.
Cover lacking forces internal rewrites.
Bribes park what pennies persuade.
Justification scales inversely with pay.
Share this: justify one dollar task.

puzzles.title: The Thin Excuse
puzzles.question: Dissonance effects grow strongest when external justification for an act is minimal — big excuses leave attitudes untouched.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Ample excuses absorb inconsistency externally; thin ones force internal revision. Justification and attitude change trade off exactly.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Large bribes and threats explain acts away, sparing beliefs; crumbs of justification leave minds to reconcile alone. Thin cover, thick change.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Thin cover forces thick change.
Excuses absorb what attitudes would carry.
Trade-offs govern justification effects.
Crumbs persuade; banquets merely pay.
Share this: act on thin excuse once.

puzzles.title: The Big Bribe
puzzles.question: Larger financial rewards for saying something you disbelieve produce proportionally larger shifts in your actual belief.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Big rewards explain the act away — no dissonance, no shift. Bribery scales inversely with persuasion of self.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Twenty dollars buys compliance while sparing conviction; one dollar buys conviction by starving excuses. Persuasion of self needs poverty, not wealth.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Wealth excuses; poverty persuades selves.
Bribery scales against belief change.
Conviction needs thin justification.
Paid minds stay put inside.
Share this: resist one big excuse.

puzzles.title: The Harsh Welcome
puzzles.question: Aronson and Mills found that volunteers enduring severe initiation to join a dull group later rated the group MORE favorably.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Effort justification: suffering for entry must mean the group is worth it. Ordeals inflate affection reliably.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Severe-initiation subjects loved the dull discussion; mild-initiation ones shrugged. Minds price memberships by pain paid, not quality received.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Pain paid prices memberships highly.
Ordeals inflate affection reliably.
Suffering for entry must mean worth.
Effort justifies what reason wouldn't.
Share this: value one hard-won group.

puzzles.title: The Easy Door
puzzles.question: Groups that admit members effortlessly inspire the deepest loyalty and highest ratings from joiners.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Costless entry breeds indifference: without suffering to justify, affection stays flat. Easy doors open onto lukewarm rooms.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Mild-initiation controls rated dull groups dully: no pain, no price inflation. Loyalty needs investment to feel valuable.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Costless entry breeds indifference reliably.
Flat affection follows painless joining.
Investment creates value feelings.
Easy doors open lukewarm rooms.
Share this: earn one membership dearly.

puzzles.title: The Spread Choice
puzzles.question: After difficult decisions, people rate chosen options higher and rejected ones lower than before choosing — the spreading of alternatives.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Choice creates dissonance; spreading resolves it: winners gilded, losers tarnished post-decision. Deciding rewrites desirability.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Brehm's appliances proved it: post-choice ratings diverge from pre-choice ones systematically. Minds flatter decisions already made.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Decisions rewrite desirability after the fact.
Winners gilded, losers tarnished routinely.
Choosing creates the dissonance spreading cures.
Minds flatter their own verdicts.
Share this: catch one spread happening.

puzzles.title: The Failed Prophecy
puzzles.question: When a cult's doomsday prophecy failed publicly, Festinger observed believers proselytizing harder rather than dispersing.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Disconfirmation plus public commitment plus social support produced intensified faith: 'When Prophecy Fails' documented it. Failed dates recruit, given sunk belief.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The Seekers' saucer never landed — and members preached more fervently after. Public commitment plus effort converts disproof into recommitment.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Disproof converts the heavily invested.
Public commitment blocks graceful exits.
Failed dates recruit under sunk belief.
Effort defends what evidence attacks.
Share this: update one failed belief.

puzzles.title: The Shattered Flock
puzzles.question: Failed prophecies invariably destroy religious movements, scattering followers permanently in every documented case.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Prophecy failure sometimes intensifies movements (Seekers, Millerites' remnants): conditions decide, not failure alone. Dispersal is one outcome among several.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. History shows recommitment, reinterpretation, and schism alongside collapse: failure's effects depend on commitment, support, and leadership. Invariably is always wrong here.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Failure's effects depend on conditions.
Recommitment rivals collapse historically.
Invariably claims fail most reliably.
Prophecies fail; movements adapt variously.
Share this: study one survived failure.

puzzles.title: The Buyer's Glow
puzzles.question: After expensive purchases, buyers rate their chosen product higher and rivals lower than beforehand — post-decision spreading in showrooms.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Costly choices demand justification: owned items gild, rejected rivals tarnish. Receipts rewrite ratings reliably.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Post-purchase spreading is showroom dissonance: money spent must mean value gained. Buyers remorse less by esteeming more.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Receipts rewrite ratings reliably.
Owned items gild post-purchase.
Costly choices demand flattering follow-ups.
Remorse fades where esteem grows.
Share this: catch one buyer's glow.

puzzles.title: The Unmoved Chooser
puzzles.question: Difficult decisions leave people's evaluations of the options essentially unchanged — attitudes stay frozen through hard choices.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Hard choices move evaluations most: near-ties generate maximum dissonance, maximum spreading. Difficulty drives revision, never stasis.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Easy choices barely ripple; agonizing ones reshape preferences deeply. Frozen attitudes contradict decades of spreading data.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Agony reshapes preferences deeply.
Near-ties generate maximum revision.
Difficulty drives change, never stasis.
Frozen attitudes contradict the data.

puzzles.title: The Forced Smile
puzzles.question: Acts performed under heavy coercion generate maximum dissonance, since the helplessness stings most sharply.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Coercion supplies complete external justification — no dissonance at all. Guns explain acts fully; attitudes rest undisturbed.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Forced compliance needs no internal revision: the gun accounts for everything. Dissonance requires felt choice, however slight.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Guns explain acts too completely.
Felt choice, however slight, is required.
Coercion spares attitudes entirely.

puzzles.title: The Cool Observer
puzzles.question: Bem's self-perception theory offered a rival account: people infer attitudes from behavior dispassionately, with no discomfort required.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False as a full replacement — Bem's account explains some findings elegantly but arousal evidence (misattribution studies) proves real discomfort operates. Rivals coexist; neither monopolizes.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Self-perception handles low-arousal cases neatly, yet physiological evidence shows genuine discomfort driving classic effects. Both mechanisms live in the literature together.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Rivals coexist in mature literatures.
Arousal evidence proves real discomfort.
Elegance never monopolizes explanation.

puzzles.title: The Trivial Clash
puzzles.question: Any inconsistency, however trivial and consequence-free, generates full-strength dissonance regardless of outcomes or self-relevance.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Cooper and Fazio showed dissonance needs aversive consequences plus felt responsibility: trivialities fizzle. Stakes and ownership gate the effect.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Mismatched socks cognitions change nothing because nothing matters and nobody chose. Consequences plus responsibility are entry tickets.

puzzles.title: The Minor Mirror
puzzles.question: Threats to trivial self-images — being once slightly late, misplacing keys — produce the strongest dissonance effects of all.
puzzles.correctExplanation: False. Aronson showed dissonance strikes hardest at central self-conceptions (competence, morality), not trivia. Mirrors crack over core reflections.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — it is false. Lateness and keys barely register; cheating and cruelty detonate. Self-concept centrality scales the blast.
puzzles.lessonContent:

puzzles.question: Smokers commonly reduce quit-pressure by disputing evidence, citing long-lived smoking relatives, and postponing action to someday.

puzzles.question: A farmer ferries a wolf, a goat, and a cabbage, taking one per trip. Wolves eat goats; goats eat cabbage. Which crosses the river first?

puzzles.title: The Repeated Block
puzzles.question: Why does 237 × 1001 equal 237237?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 1001 = 1000 + 1 — multiplying adds the number to its thousand-shifted self: abc000 + abc = abcabc. Structure, never coincidence.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 1001 equals 1000 plus one. Coincidence, rounding, and magic miss it: 237×1000 = 237000, plus 237 more. Addition explains repetition exactly.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Structure explains repetition exactly.
Thousand-plus-one duplicates blocks.
Addition, never magic, repeats digits.
1001 splits usefully always.

puzzles.title: The Six-Ones
puzzles.question: 111,111 factors with a familiar 4-digit number. Which one?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 1001 — 111,111 = 3 × 37 × 1001. Six ones hide the famous thousand.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is 1001. Test small factors: 3 gives 37037, and 37 × 1001 completes it. Ones factor into familiar thousands.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Ones factor into familiar thousands.
Small factors first, always.
Six ones hide famous thousands.
37037 splits revealingly.

puzzles.title: The Odd Palindrome
puzzles.question: Four mirrored numbers face the eleven-test; three pass while one fails. Which palindrome breaks ranks?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 12321 — alternating difference 1−2+3−2+1... precisely |2+3−4| = 1, not a multiple of 11. The others divide cleanly (1221, 1111, 2222).
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 12321. Alternating-sum test: 13431 (diff 0), 12221 (0), 24442 (0) all pass; 12321 gives remainder 1. One rebel among compliant palindromes.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Alternating sums test elevens fast.
Zero difference means divisible here.
Rebels hide among compliant shapes.
Palindromes usually — not always — comply.

puzzles.title: The Quarter Hundred
puzzles.question: Is 1,234,575 divisible by 25?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Yes — 25 divides exactly the endings 00, 25, 50, 75: 75 qualifies. Hundreds never matter.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is yes, ends in 75. Quarters of hundreds decide: 00/25/50/75 pass, all else fails. Endings rule twenty-fives completely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Quarters of hundreds decide fully.
00-25-50-75 pass; rest fail.
Endings rule twenty-fives completely.
Hundreds never matter here.

puzzles.title: The 125 Test
puzzles.question: A mill bags flour in 125-unit sacks, rejecting partial sacks. Which harvest weight bags perfectly?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 7,750 — 125 × 62 exactly. Thousands never matter; final trios decide eighths of thousands.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 7,750. Test endings: only multiples of 125 in the final three digits qualify — 750 passes, 755/700/705 fail. Trios decide 125s.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Final trios decide 125s fully.
Thousands never matter here.
750 passes; neighbors fail.
Eighths of thousands need trios.

puzzles.title: The Prime Test
puzzles.question: Is 97 prime?
puzzles.correctExplanation: Yes — test primes through √97 ≈ 9.8: 2, 3, 5, 7 all fail to divide. Primality confirmed by exhaustion.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is yes, it is prime. Check 7 (91, 98 bracket), 13 (too big alone... 13×7 = 91 ≠ 97), evenness, fives, threes: all fail. Exhaustion proves primality here.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Exhaustion proves small primalities.
Test primes through square roots.
Brackets (91, 98) exclude seven.
Ninety-seven stands undivided.

puzzles.title: The Ninety-One Trap
puzzles.question: Is 91 prime?
puzzles.correctExplanation: No — 91 = 7 × 13, the classic prime impostor. Ends-in-1 numbers deserve factor checks.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is no, 7 times 13. Primality claims fail: 7×13 = 91 exactly. Impostors end in 1, 3, 7, 9 — check small factors always.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Impostors end in 1, 3, 7, 9.
Check small factors unfailingly.
91 factors as seven-thirteen.
Prime looks deceive regularly.

puzzles.title: The Sum Clue
puzzles.question: A number's digit sum is 27. Which divisibility is guaranteed?
puzzles.correctExplanation: By 3 and 9 — 27 splits by both (9 and 3), and digit-sum rules inherit downward. Sums guarantee divisibility.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is by 3 and 9. Twenty-seven's factors transfer: whatever the sum allows, the number obeys. Sevens, elevens, and nones miss it.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Sums transfer factors downward.
Twenty-seven splits both ways.
Guarantees ride digit totals.
Inherit divisibility from sums.

puzzles.title: The Common Multiple
puzzles.question: What is the smallest positive integer divisible by every number from 1 through 10?
puzzles.correctExplanation: 2520 — 2³ × 3² × 5 × 7 covers every prime power through 10. Least common multiple by max exponents.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is 2520. Take highest prime powers ≤10 (8, 9, 5, 7) and multiply: 8×9×5×7 = 2520. Halves and doubles miss both ways.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Max exponents build least multiples.
Prime powers through ten suffice.
2520 covers one through ten.
Multiply peaks, never all numbers.

puzzles.title: The Supersonic Fallacy
puzzles.question: The sunk-cost fallacy is nicknamed the Concorde fallacy after the Anglo-French jetliner program continued despite mounting losses.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Concorde flew on after economics failed: prestige plus spent billions overruled arithmetic. Nicknames commemorate famous traps.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. The jet lost money nearly every year yet flew for decades: abandoning billions felt worse than losing millions yearly. History's costliest loyalty program.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Prestige plus spent billions overrule arithmetic.
Loyalty programs cost history dearly.
Nicknames commemorate famous traps well.
Abandoning feels worse than bleeding.

puzzles.title: The Sacrifice Ledger
puzzles.question: During Vietnam, leaders invoked past American sacrifices as reasons to continue fighting rather than withdraw.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Fallen soldiers became arguments against exit: McNamara and successors priced credibility in sunk lives. Ledgers of the dead funded further dying.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. 'Their sacrifice must not be in vain' converted losses into reasons for losses: escalation's moral arithmetic. Sacrifice-ledgers fund folly reliably.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Fallen become arguments against exit.
Vain-avoidance funds further dying.
Moral arithmetic escalates reliably.
Ledgers of dead demand living interest.

puzzles.title: The Dollar Spiral
puzzles.question: In Shubik's dollar auction — $1 auctioned to the highest bidder, runner-up also paying — final prices routinely exceed one dollar.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Top two bidders both pay, so quitting wastes bids already placed: spirals past face value are standard. Auction design manufactures escalation.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Runner-up-pays converts auctions into traps: each bid protects prior bids, climbing past the prize. Classrooms pay $5 for $1 routinely.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Top-two-pays manufactures spirals reliably.
Protecting bids climbs past prizes.
Design traps bidders structurally here.
Face values fall to sunk logic.

puzzles.title: The Responsibility Trap
puzzles.question: Staw found that personal responsibility for an initial decision deepens commitment to failing courses — choosers escalate more than inheritors.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Self-justification fuels escalation: admitting error costs more than funding failure. Choosers defend; inheritors cut.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Responsibility binds: decision-makers double down where successors walk away. Ego invests alongside capital, then outspends it.
puzzles.lessonContent:
Ego invests alongside capital always.
Choosers defend; inheritors cut cleanly.
Admitting error costs more than funding.
Responsibility binds decisions tightly.

puzzles.title: The Good Money
puzzles.question: 'Throwing good money after bad' describes investing further specifically to justify or rescue past spending.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. The idiom names escalation precisely: fresh funds drafted to vindicate sunk ones. Rescue missions for money already gone.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Good money follows bad hoping vindication: each round defends the last. Idioms encode economics folk-wisely.
puzzles.lessonContent:

Rescue missions chase gone money.
Idioms encode economics folk-wisely.
Good follows bad downhill reliably.

puzzles.title: The Justified Hole
puzzles.question: The need to justify past choices to oneself and others deepens commitment to failing courses of action.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Self-justification converts errors into identities: abandoning means confessing. Holes deepen to protect diggers' pride.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Dissonance funds failing projects: quitting indicts the quitter. Pride digs where arithmetic would fill.

Quitting indicts quitters painfully.
Errors become identities needing defense.
Justification deepens holes steadily.

puzzles.title: The Imagined Funeral
puzzles.question: Klein's premortem — imagining a project has already failed, then explaining why — reduces escalation by licensing doubt in advance.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Prospective hindsight legitimizes dissent before commitment hardens: funerals imagined prevent real ones.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Premortems license what meetings punish: voicing failure modes early, when exits stay cheap. Doubt in advance beats regret after.

Funerals imagined prevent real ones.
Dissent licensed early stays cheap.
Hindsight prospected prevents escalation.

puzzles.title: The Exit Contract
puzzles.question: Preset kill criteria — exit rules written before investing — reliably curb escalation by deciding in calm weather.
puzzles.correctExplanation: True. Ulysses contracts bind future selves: calm-weather rules override storm-weather rationalizing. Precommitment beats willpower.
puzzles.incorrectExplanation: It is true. Kill criteria decide exits before attachment forms: storms later cannot rewrite calm contracts. Decide cold to quit hot correctly.

Precommitment beats willpower reliably.
Decide cold to quit hot correctly.
Exits preset survive attachment.
